Everything under this heading documents the 0.16.0-dev line: the master branch of the Tau repository (published on GitHub as the rust-rewrite branch of jmccardle/tau), version string 0.16.0.dev0, protocol 1. It is not on PyPI, it has no release tag, and its interfaces can still change. The released Tau is v0.15.0, the Python five-package line; use that for anything you depend on.

0.16 is a rewrite, not an upgrade. A sans-IO Rust core (crates/) sits under a Python driver, hooks, providers, tools and frontends (python/tau), shipped as one package, ffwf-tau, that you import tau. The design is a session as a tree of nodes, with cursors that walk it, and steps that hooks can change at fixed points.

Documented against: commit c439c401 of master, v0.15.0 plus 276 commits; Cargo.toml says 0.16.0-dev.0; tau --version prints tau 0.16.0.dev0 (protocol 1).

docs.title: What state it is in
docs.text:
The project plan has ten phases; at this commit phases 0 to 6 are done, phases 7 (the wire, the shared start, the API docs) and 8 (frontends, tools, standard extensions) are in progress, and phase 9 (the release: wheels beyond Linux x86_64, the PyPI workflow, release notes) has not started.

Built (this commit) Not built Rust core, session store, Python bindings Wheels for macOS, Windows or aarch64; Linux x86_64 only, and the base tools are Linux-only Providers: OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini, a scripted mock PyPI release (no 0.16 wheel exists) Base tools read, write, edit, grep, find, bash Image input, constrained decoding, a models.dev catalog, code mode, background tools The tau program: terminal UI, tau -p, --json, --answer --mode rpc over stdio (the Tectum contract), --mode repl, --bus (NATS) tau serve (JSON-RPC over a WebSocket on a Unix socket), --schema Per-run tool lists (--tools, --no-tools, --exclude-tools) Built-in extensions: retry, @file attachments, prompt templates and skills, usage and cost, compaction, prune, permissions, sub-agents (off by default), step limit HTML export, the JMFTS session store Project trust (tau trust), tau config check, layered config, .env A converter for 0.15 session files (there will not be one) A ratatui example client in examples/ratatui Changes in the sibling clients (tau-code, tau-search), which sync after 0.16.0

What changed from 0.15 says what each 0.15 capability became.

docs.text: Page Covers Quickstart Build it, configure one model, chat, list and export sessions, serve a session Writing an extension Tools, commands, options, hooks, and where extensions load from Operating it $TAU_HOME, config layers, project trust, serving, CI and wheels Reference The tau command line, the public Python API groups, the wire protocol What changed from 0.15 Built, changed, dropped and planned, per capability

docs.title: What changed from 0.15
docs.text:
Unreleased

Describes 0.16.0-dev (commit c439c401) against the released v0.15.0. The Tau repository keeps a ledger, docs/from-0.15.md, with one row per 0.15 capability; it was written on 2026-10-31 and some of its rows are older than the code (for example it lists tau ext and tau serve as missing; both now exist). Where the ledger and the current --help disagree, this page follows the code. Built means present at this commit and tested; planned means a document says it is coming; dropped is by design.

(a switch); exit codes 0/1/2/3/130 built, changed --mode json --json (the wire's events) built, changed --mode rpc (stdio JSON-RPC, 45 verbs) tau serve: JSON-RPC over WebSocket on a Unix socket; stdio is planned after 0.16.0 changed; stdio planned --mode repl none dropped (plan.md) --bus (NATS), the nats_bus extension none not planned for 0.16 --ext-config NAME:KEY=VALUE --set EXTENSION.FIELD=VALUE, TAU_SETTINGS, tau config set built, changed --ui-defaults --answer EXTENSION[:TEXT]=VALUE built, changed --max-turns --set step_limit.limit=N; stopping there exits 3 built, changed --tools, --no-tools, --exclude-tools, --no-builtin-tools none; tau ext disable base_tools turns the base tools off deferred to after 0.16.0 --provider, --thinking provider key and provider options in config dropped --prompt-template, --skill and their --no- forms files in $TAU_HOME/.tau prompts/ and skills/; disable the skills extension changed --store file\|jmfts, import/export session none; the JMFTS replica comes after 0.16.0 not built --export-html tau export (Markdown) HTML planned later --connect, tau serve --listen/--tail/--web-root attaching is automatic; tau serve --socket --tail, web client not built tau ext list/enable/disable/authorize/revoke tau ext list/enable/disable; trust is tau trust built, changed (none) tau config check/set, tau trust, tau sessions, tau export, tau context, tau --version new

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: Area 0.16 State API keys Never discovered by default: a model names its api_key_env changed (0.15 had per-vendor defaults) Project config Gated by tau trust with hashes of the exact files new Provider retry Built-in retry wrapper, on by default (load: {retry: false} turns it off) built Compaction, prune Built-in extensions (/compact, /prune, proactive trigger on context_window) built Permissions Built-in permissions extension: ask, allow, deny rules; asks nothing until configured built Sub-agents Built-in agents extension, off by default (tau ext enable agents); runs in-process as cursors built @file, prompt templates, skills Built-in attachments and skills; no images; templates support $ARGUMENTS, $1..$9 only built, reduced Usage and cost usage extension (status line, /usage, price) built Steering and follow-up queues, step debugger suspensions, entry annotations none dropped by design Image input, constrained decoding, models.dev catalog, code mode, background tools none not built; listed as post-0.16 candidates Windows and macOS none yet planned (phase 9)

docs.title: Things that still disagree
docs.text:
• The ledger docs/from-0.15.md predates the current CLI (see above) and is not regenerated.
  • The Tectum integration targets 0.15's stdio RPC and --no-tools; neither exists in 0.16 and both are planned only after 0.16.0 (docs/plan.md, "After 0.16.0").

docs.title: Writing an extension (0.16 preview)
docs.text:
Unreleased, and not the 0.15 API

This is the 0.16.0-dev extension model. It shares no code with 0.15's ExtensionAPI; a 0.15 extension does not load in 0.16 and there is no compatibility shim. For 0.15 see Extensions. Source: docs/guide/extensions.md at commit c439c401, whose examples the repository runs as tests.

An extension is a Python object with a name and any of:

  • tools the model can call,
  • commands a person types as /name,
  • options, settings kept in the config,
  • hooks, functions Tau calls at fixed points of a step.

It can also show a status on a cursor and ask whoever is watching a question. Extension objects come from import tau; there is no ExtensionAPI object to receive.

docs.title: A complete extension
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from tau import Body, CallDraft, Cursor, NodeHandle, ToolError


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Options:
    max_chars: Annotated[int, "longest text the shout tool takes"] = 40


class Shouter:
    name = "shouter"
    options = Options

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.tools = (self.shout,)
        self.commands = (self.count,)

    def shout(self, text: Annotated[str, "what to say"], node: NodeHandle) -> str:
        """Return the text in capitals."""
        longest = node.options().max_chars
        if len(text) > longest:
            raise ToolError(f"say at most {longest} characters")
        return text.upper()

    async def count(self, cursor: Cursor) -> str:
        """Say how many nodes are on this branch."""
        mine = await cursor.ask("Count only the messages you sent?", bool)
        nodes = cursor.walk()
        if mine:
            nodes = [n for n in nodes if isinstance(n.body, Body.User)]
        cursor.show(f"{len(nodes)} counted")
        return f"{len(nodes)} nodes"

    async def pre_tool(self, node: NodeHandle, call: CallDraft) -> str | None:
        verdict = await node.ask(f"let the model call {call.tool}?", Literal["yes", "no"])
        return None if verdict == "yes" else "the user said no"


extensions = [Shouter()]

A module with a name is itself the extension; otherwise it defines extensions = [...], a non-empty list. Save the file as shouter.py and load it for one run with tau ext list -e shouter.py or tau -e shouter.py ....

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: A tool is a plain function in tools. The name is the function name, the description is its docstring (no docstring: DefinitionError at load), and the parameters are a JSON Schema built from the type hints. Allowed hints: str, int, float, bool, Literal, list[T], T | None, pathlib.Path, and the named types Model, CursorId, LabelName, NodeId. Annotated[T, "text"] adds a description. The function returns a str. Raise ToolError to tell the model why it failed. Sync tools run in a worker thread; async ones on the loop. Tau fills in NodeHandle, TreeHandle and Progress parameters by annotation and hides them from the model. Tool names are not namespaced; two tools with one name are an error.

docs.title: Commands and options
docs.text:
A command is a function in commands, run as /name; its docstring is the help and its parameters are the arguments. One that takes a Cursor runs as a step of that cursor. Two extensions with the same command name make the bare name ambiguous; the qualified form /shouter:count always works.

options names a frozen dataclass with plain defaults. Values come from extensions.<name> in the config files, tau config set shouter.max_chars=80, --set shouter.max_chars=80 for one run, or /config shouter max_chars=80 in a session.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: An async method named for its point. A cursor hook is hook(cursor, subject), a tool hook hook(node, call). In the order a step reaches them: pre_step, pre_input, pre_sample, pre_reply, post_reply, pre_tool, pre_result, post_result, post_step. Returning None carries on; returning a string stops the step with that reason (for a tool hook the string becomes the call's error). An exception fails the step. A tool hook may rewrite call.args_raw or set call.outcome to answer the call.

docs.title: Where Tau finds extensions
docs.text:
In load order: built-in (agents, attachments, base_tools, compaction, permissions, prune, skills, step_limit, usage, and retry for the provider wrapper), installed packages in the tau.extensions entry-point group (the value is a module), user drop-ins in $TAU_HOME/extensions/, project drop-ins in .tau/extensions/ (only after tau trust), then -e PATH|KEY (naming it is the consent). A later source with the same key shadows an earlier one. tau ext list [--json] shows every source and why it is on or off; tau ext enable KEY and tau ext disable KEY write the load key of your config. A source that fails to load stops Tau from starting rather than carrying on unguarded.

The six base tools (read, write, edit, grep, find, bash) come from the built-in base_tools; tau ext disable base_tools starts sessions without them.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Drive the extension with a scripted provider (an object with name, check, aclose and an async-generator sample) through Driver, Session.create and a Client, with no network. The repository's guide shows a complete runnable test; the Harness protocol in tests/behavior is how Tau tests itself.

docs.title: Operating Tau 0.16 (preview)
docs.text:
Unreleased

0.16.0-dev, commit c439c401. Operations for the released line are in the v0.15.0 DevOps Manual. Nothing here is packaged for deployment yet.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Only from source (see the quickstart): Python 3.12 or later and a Rust toolchain. The package is ffwf-tau, the import is tau, the command is tau. Runtime dependencies are httpx, websockets and textual. The planned wheels are one cp312-abi3 wheel for every GIL build from 3.12 and a version-specific cp314t wheel for free-threaded 3.14. Only Linux x86_64 is built or tested; the base tools use /proc and are Linux-only. macOS, aarch64, Windows and the PyPI publish workflow are phase 9, not started.

docs.title: What lives where
docs.text: $TAU_HOME (default ~/.tau): config.json, trusted.json, sessions/ (one directory per session), extensions/, serve/ (sockets and records of tau serve), prompts/, skills/, themes/, and an AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md for every session. Keep it private: Tau refuses to approve a project while $TAU_HOME or trusted.json is writable by other users. Sessions are not 0.15's JSONL files: they are a checksummed record log plus a scratchpad file per session, and Tau 0.16 ignores 0.15 session files.

docs.title: Configuration layers
docs.text: Nearest wins: user ($TAU_HOME/config.json), project (.tau/config.json in a trusted project), session (--set, --system-prompt, and the TAU_SETTINGS JSON environment variable). Objects merge by key, lists and scalars replace, null removes. Top-level keys: models, default_model, extensions, load, system_prompt, tui. An unknown key is an error with a suggestion. tau config check [--show MODEL] [--clean] [--purge EXT] [--layer user|project] validates; tau config set EXT.FIELD=VALUE writes an option. API keys are never in config: api_key_env names the variable, read when a sample is made. A literal api_key works but warns. Unlike 0.15, there is no per-vendor default environment variable: a hosted model must say which variable holds its key.

docs.title: Project trust
docs.text: A project's .tau/ can set base_url (where your key is sent) and run Python, so Tau does not use it until you run tau trust [DIR], which prints the config (keys blanked), the extension files and the names, not values, of the .env variables, and then pins the exact bytes of config.json, .env, extensions/, SYSTEM.md, prompts/ and skills/. Any change untrusts the project. With no terminal (a script, tau serve -d) an untrusted project is refused and the message names tau trust.

docs.title: Serving
docs.text: tau serve [-d] [--json] [--socket PATH] [--stop] [--schema] runs one session on a Unix socket (file permissions are the only authentication) speaking JSON-RPC 2.0 over WebSocket. -d detaches; the record is also $TAU_HOME/serve/<id>.json. A session a server holds is Leased to it: tau, tau -p and tau export attach or read; to work on a copy use --fork. A session held by another process is otherwise refused. tau serve --schema prints the JSON Schema of the protocol; the TypeScript clients are generated from it. This is not 0.15's tau serve: there is no --listen, --connect, --tail or --web-root, and no stdio RPC mode.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: The repository's CI (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml) runs scripts/check.sh: rustfmt, clippy, cargo tests, a maturin build, rule lints, a complexity ratchet, stubtest, ruff, pyright, pytest (the behavior suite runs twice: local, then over a socket), and checks that the generated API docs, the protocol guide, the wire schema and the diagrams are current and that every example in the guides runs. The same script (scripts/check.sh) runs locally.

docs.title: Errors you will meet
docs.text: tau: model 'x' is not in your config (run tau config check); project is not trusted (run tau trust); session ... is in use by another process (fork it or attach); an extension that fails to load stops startup and names the way past it (tau ext disable KEY or --no-extensions).

docs.title: Quickstart (0.16 preview)
docs.text:
Unreleased

This is Tau 0.16.0-dev, built from the repository's master branch. For the released Tau, see the v0.15.0 quickstart. Every command below was run against commit c439c401 with a temporary TAU_HOME and the mock model, which needs no server and no API key.

docs.title: Build it
docs.text:
There is no 0.16 release on PyPI, so you build from a checkout. You need Python 3.12 or later and Rust (rustup, cargo 1.89 or later).

git clone https://github.com/jmccardle/tau && cd tau
git checkout rust-rewrite
python3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install --group dev           # pip 25.1 or later
VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/.venv .venv/bin/maturin develop --release
source .venv/bin/activate                   # puts `tau` on your PATH
tau --version                               # tau 0.16.0.dev0 (protocol 1)

Everything Tau keeps lives in $TAU_HOME, which is ~/.tau unless you set it (an absolute path, or one that starts with ~).

docs.title: A config with one model
docs.text:
$TAU_HOME/config.json names your models. A group holds what its models share (here the server); a model's qualified name is the group, a colon and the model: local:qwen.

{
  "default_model": "local:qwen",
  "models": {
    "local": {
      "base_url": "http://localhost:8100/v1",
      "models": { "qwen": { "model": "qwen3-27b" } }
    },
    "mock": {
      "provider": "mock",
      "models": { "echo": { "model": "echo" } }
    }
  }
}

local is any server that speaks the OpenAI chat API (llama.cpp, vLLM, a hosted service). For a hosted one add "api_key_env": "NAME_OF_YOUR_KEY_VARIABLE" to the group; the config names the variable and never holds the key. provider is openai (the default), anthropic, gemini or mock. Check the file:

tau config check
tau config check --show local:qwen

check prints nothing when the config is sound, and one line per problem otherwise.

docs.title: Ask once
docs.text:
tau -p sends one message, prints the answer on standard output and exits. -m picks the model, -n names the session. The session is kept.

tau -p -m mock:echo -n quickstart "hello from a script"
# mock: hello from a script

Standard input that is not a terminal follows the words after a blank line, so git diff | tau -p "review this" works. Exit status: 0 finished, 1 failure, 2 usage error, 3 stopped before finishing (a step limit, a halting hook), 130 interrupted. --json prints the session's events one JSON object per line, the same objects the wire sends. --set step_limit.limit=5 changes an extension option for one run. A question an extension asks (a permission) has nobody to answer it under -p and is declined unless a rule answers: --answer permissions=yes.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
tau with no -p opens the terminal UI. -c continues the newest session of this directory, -r chooses one, --session REF opens one (attaching if a tau serve holds it), and --theme NAME picks mocha (default), latte, gruvbox or ansi. Enter sends, Ctrl+J starts a new line, Esc aborts the step, Ctrl+G shows the tree, Ctrl+Q quits.

tau -m mock:echo

docs.title: Look at what you did
docs.text:
tau sessions                      # this directory's sessions, newest first
tau sessions --json               # one object per line
tau export quickstart | head -n 12  # a session as Markdown (-o FILE, --thinking)
tau context                       # what a new session would be told, with sizes
tau ext list                      # every extension source, and why it is on or off

docs.title: Serve a session
docs.text:
tau serve -d --json --session quickstart
tau serve --stop --session quickstart

The first prints one JSON object: the socket, the server pid, the session, its cwd, the protocol and version. Python programs connect with RemoteClient; other languages follow the wire protocol.

docs.title: Verified and not verified
docs.text: All commands above except the build, git clone, tau (the interactive UI) and the local:qwen model (which needs your server) were run by the repository's own documentation test (scripts/guide_examples.py) during this pass. The build steps are quoted from the repository's CLAUDE.md and were not re-run here: an existing .venv at that commit was used.

docs.title: Reference (0.16 preview)
docs.text:
Unreleased

0.16.0-dev, commit c439c401. The released reference is Tau v0.15.0 Reference.

docs.title: The tau command line
docs.text:
Checked against tau --help and each subcommand's --help at this commit.

tau [options] [MESSAGE ...]          open the terminal UI; with -p send MESSAGE, print the answer, exit
tau COMMAND ...                      config | ext | sessions | export | context | serve | trust

The first argument decides: a subcommand's name runs it, anything else is the launch command line (tau -p sessions sends the word "sessions").

Flag Meaning -p, --print send MESSAGE (stdin after a blank line if not a terminal), print the answer; exit 0 done, 1 failed, 2 usage, 3 stopped before finishing, 130 interrupted -m, --model NAME model of a new session (default: default_model) --json print the session's events, one JSON object per line --answer EXTENSION[:TEXT]=VALUE answer questions extensions ask (repeatable; first match wins; no match declines) --theme NAME terminal UI theme for this run (not with -p) -c, --continue open the newest session of this directory -r, --resume choose a session to open (not with -p) --session REF open a session: path, id, name or id prefix --fork REF[:NODE] start a new session as a copy of one walk of REF --no-session keep the session in memory -n, --name NAME name the session --session-dir DIR keep and find sessions in DIR (default $TAU_HOME/sessions) --system-prompt TEXT, --append-system-prompt TEXT, -nc/--no-context-files system prompt controls (an error with -c, -r, --session, --fork, except -nc) -e, --extension PATH\|KEY load this extension even if off (repeatable) --no-extensions skip packages and drop-ins; the built-ins still follow load --set EXTENSION.FIELD=VALUE extension option for this run (repeatable); load.KEY=true\|false too --verbose report the start, and under -p each node, on standard error -v, --version print the version and the protocol

Subcommands: tau config check [--show MODEL] [--clean] [--purge EXT] [--layer user|project], tau config set EXT.FIELD=VALUE..., tau ext list [-e] [--no-extensions] [--json], tau ext enable KEY, tau ext disable KEY, tau sessions [--all] [--json], tau sessions name REF [NAME], tau export REF [-o FILE] [--thinking], tau context [--show] [prompt flags], tau trust [DIR], tau serve [session and extension flags] [--socket PATH] [-d | --stop | --schema] [--json]. There is no --mode, --store, --provider, --thinking, --tools family, --bus or --connect; see what changed.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: TAU_HOME (state directory), TAU_SETTINGS (JSON session settings with load and extensions), and whatever variables your models' api_key_env name.

docs.title: The Python API
docs.text:
from tau import Name reaches every public name; the other public modules are tau.cli, tau.commandline, tau.tui and tau.trace. Everything else is private (underscore-named). The pages below are generated from docstrings, one per group:

Overview | Extensions | Tools | Records | Clients | Events | Sessions | The wire | Driver | Providers | Step machine | Config | Errors | Terminal UI | Tracing

docs.title: The wire protocol
docs.text: The wire protocol is generated from the JSON Schema that tau serve --schema prints (protocol number 1, matched exactly by the server's hello).

Generated from the docstrings of Tau 0.16.0-dev (commit c439c401) by scripts/api_docs.py in the Tau repository. Not the 0.15 API.

docs.title: Tau 0.16 preview API: Writing a frontend
docs.text:
Unreleased

Generated from the docstrings of Tau 0.16.0-dev (commit c439c401) by scripts/api_docs.py in the Tau repository. Not the 0.15 API.

docs.title: Writing a frontend
docs.text:
A frontend holds a Client, in this process or over the wire, and reads the line a person typed.

Names: Client, CommandFailed, LocalClient, Parsed, RemoteClient, UnknownCommand, commandline.STDIN, commandline.completions, commandline.parse, commandline.value, commandline.values

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
class Client(AsyncIterator[Event], Protocol)
    id: str

What a frontend holds. Iterating it yields the events: first a snapshot (a CursorView per open cursor, a CursorGone per closed one, then Labels), then changes as they happen, until the driver stops (the stream ends), or the driver fails or the client is CutOff for falling behind (it raises ConnectionError). Every call raises ConnectionError once the driver has failed or stopped, or the client has been closed or cut off.

docs.title: Client.input
docs.text:
async def input(self, cursor: int, text: str) -> int

Add text to the cursor's scratchpad as this client's input; returns the item.

docs.title: Client.send
docs.text:
async def send(self, cursor: int, text: str) -> int

input with auto-step on.

docs.title: Client.step
docs.text:
async def step(self, cursor: int) -> None

Start a step on a cursor at rest; Busy otherwise.

docs.title: Client.go_to
docs.text:
async def go_to(self, cursor: int, to: int) -> None

Move the cursor to node to, aborting a busy step (which declines its open questions).

docs.title: Client.remove_item
docs.text:
async def remove_item(self, cursor: int, item: int) -> None

Take back a pending input this client added to cursor (input or send): it is removed from the scratchpad before the cursor delivers it. LookupError once it is delivered, or if there is no such item on the cursor; PermissionError for an item another client or an extension added. Wakes nothing and does not turn auto-step off.

docs.title: Client.set_auto
docs.text:
async def set_auto(self, cursor: int, on: bool) -> None

Turn cursor's auto-step on or off; on wakes it.

docs.title: Client.abort
docs.text:
async def abort(self, cursor: int) -> None

Abort the cursor's step and decline its open questions.

docs.title: Client.open
docs.text:
async def open(self, at: int) -> int

Open a cursor at node at; it wakes. Returns its id.

docs.title: Client.close_cursor
docs.text:
async def close_cursor(self, cursor: int) -> None

Close the cursor (D17): abort its step as abort does, wait for it to rest, drop its pending items, and close it. Clients are sent a CursorGone. Its id, last node and labels stay; reopen restarts from them. CursorClosed if it is already closed.

docs.title: Client.reopen
docs.text:
async def reopen(self, cursor: int) -> int

Open a new cursor at the closed cursor's last node, and move each of its labels onto it. Returns the new id. ValueError if cursor is open, NoSuchCursor if it was never opened.

docs.title: Client.set_label
docs.text:
async def set_label(self, cursor: int, label: str) -> None

Put label on cursor; a label set elsewhere moves.

docs.title: Client.remove_label
docs.text:
async def remove_label(self, label: str) -> None

Remove label; NoSuchLabel if there is none.

docs.title: Client.watch
docs.text:
async def watch(self, cursors: Collection[int]) -> None

Hear the Live of exactly these cursors from now on (a call replaces the last), starting with what each sample in flight has streamed that is not in the tree yet.

docs.title: Client.answer
docs.text:
async def answer(self, question: int, value: object) -> None

Answer an open question with a decoded JSON value; None declines. ValueError if the value is wrong (the question stays open), LookupError if the question is closed or unknown (the first good answer wins), PermissionError if it is for another client.

docs.title: Client.close
docs.text:
async def close(self) -> None

Disconnect: the stream ends and the client is no longer connected.

docs.title: Client.node
docs.text:
async def node(self, id: int) -> Node

The node with this id; NoSuchNode if there is none.

docs.title: Client.nodes
docs.text:
async def nodes(self, start: int, limit: int) -> list[Node]

Up to limit nodes from id start, in id order; none past the end. Ids are dense and a node never changes, so a tree is read in ranges. ValueError for a negative start or limit.

docs.title: Client.walk
docs.text:
async def walk(self, id: int) -> list[Node]

The nodes from the root to id.

docs.title: Client.children
docs.text:
async def children(self, id: int) -> list[int]

The ids of the children of node id, in append order.

docs.title: Client.commands
docs.text:
async def commands(self) -> tuple[Form, ...]

Each command's form: its name, description and argument schema (named types with their "format", each default), fixed until the driver reloads. If some extension has options there is one more, config, whose one argument is the extension; it is changed with configure, not run.

docs.title: Client.run
docs.text:
async def run(self, cursor: int, command: str, args: Mapping[str, object]) -> str | None

Run /command ("note", or "a:note", the extension's qualified name) with decoded JSON args on cursor; returns the command's result (None if it has none) once it has finished. CommandFailed (its message is the failure as "Type: msg") if it raised, or was aborted; it is raised as soon as the command raises, even when the command's step has not yet ended: the cursor may still be busy for a moment while the step ends, and a retry then gets Busy. A command's progress and cursor.tell arrive as Notices. LookupError for an unknown command or a bare name two extensions share ("/note is two commands: /a:note, /b:note"), ValueError naming the problem for arguments that fit no parameter (the values are checked with the session, "new" last), Busy for a command that runs as a step of the cursor when it is not at rest.

docs.title: Client.options
docs.text:
async def options(self, cursor: int, extension: str) -> Form

extension's options as they stand at cursor: a form whose schema has every option, each default the value now. ConfigError if it has no options.

docs.title: Client.configure
docs.text:
async def configure(
    self,
    cursor: int,
    extension: str,
    values: Mapping[str, object],
    *,
    save: bool = False,
) -> None

Change the options named in values (decoded JSON) of extension on cursor's branch: a step of the cursor writes a Config node. With save, the server also writes the user's config file (extensions.<name>), which every session reads: the options in values and those a Config node on the branch set, wherever they differ from the file's (options equal to the file's stay untouched; values may be {}; options only the user, project or command-line layers set are not copied). A client needs no access to that file. ConfigError for an extension without options, or values its options type refuses (or, with save, a driver with no user config), Busy unless the cursor is at rest; nothing is written then, neither node nor file.

docs.title: Client.complete
docs.text:
async def complete(self, cursor: int, named: str, prefix: str) -> list[str]

The values of a named type ("path", "model", "cursor", "label", "node"; the "format" of a schema) that start with prefix, as cursor sees them. Paths are the driver's machine's, relative to its working directory.

docs.title: Client.parse_line
docs.text:
async def parse_line(self, cursor: int, line: str) -> Parsed

commandline.parse of line with this driver's forms and the options forms cursor sees: the command, its arguments, and the required parameters still missing. UnknownCommand if no command has the name (send the line as text), ValueError for a line that cannot be read, plain LookupError for a bare name two extensions share.

docs.title: Client.complete_line
docs.text:
async def complete_line(self, cursor: int, line: str) -> list[str]

commandline.completions of line on the driver: what could finish its last word, in one call.

docs.title: CommandFailed
docs.text:
class CommandFailed(RuntimeError)

A command raised, or returned what is not a str or None. The message is the failure as "Type: msg". Client.run raises it as soon as the command raises; an aborted one raises it too. A command raises it itself to refuse (its arguments, say), with a message for the person: the caller gets that message as written, with no traceback, and a command that takes a Cursor does not fail its step for it.

Models, the config files, trust, extension loading, the system prompt.

Ask = Callable[[str], bool]

A yes-or-no question put to the person: takes the question, returns the answer.

docs.title: ConfigError
docs.text:
class ConfigError(ValueError)

A Config's data that does not name a model, a model that is not in the config, an invalid resolved model, a key that cannot be read, or options that do not fit their extension: an extension with none, an unknown option, a wrong type, a missing required one, or a refusal by the options type's own __post_init__.

docs.title: ConfigProblem
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ConfigProblem
    severity: Severity
    message: str
    source: str | None = None
    path: str = ''
    line: int | None = None
    column: int | None = None

One thing wrong (or suspicious) in the config layers.

source is the file path or "session"; path the dotted location inside it (models.free_tokens.models.gpt-6-sol.modle); line and column are set for JSON syntax errors. The message never holds an API key.

docs.title: ContextFileError
docs.text:
class ContextFileError(ConfigError)

A context file that was found and cannot be used. The message names the path and the cause, and says how to start without context files.

docs.title: DotenvError
docs.text:
class DotenvError(ValueError)

A .env line that is not KEY=value; the message names the file and line, not the value.

docs.title: ExtensionLoadError
docs.text:
class ExtensionLoadError(ImportError)

One or more extension sources did not load: the message is every failure (what failed, its source, the underlying error, and the command that gets past it), and sources their ExtensionSource records. The first underlying exception is __cause__.

docs.text: def __init__(self, message: str, sources: Sequence['ExtensionSource'] = ()) -> None

docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ExtensionSource
    key: str
    state: SourceState
    kind: SourceKind
    origin: str
    detail: str | None = None
    extensions: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    commands: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    tools: tuple[str, ...] = ()

One row of tau ext list: the source's key, its state (always: tau and session_name; on; off; shadowed, by what; failed; untrusted), its kind (built-in, package, user, project, explicit for -e, or load for a load key that no source has), origin (where it is) and detail (why it is off, shadowed, untrusted or failed). extensions are the names of the extensions it provides, commands their commands' qualified names and tools their tools' names; all empty unless it is on.

One config layer: the Path of a file, or a LayerText already read.

docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LayerText

    text: str

A layer already read: its text and the source (file path) problems name. Accepted wherever a layer takes a Path, so a caller that read and showed the text reads exactly that text.

docs.title: LoadedConfig
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LoadedConfig
    catalog: ModelCatalog
    environ: Mapping[str, str]
    project: Trusted | None
    home: Path
    user: UserConfig

The result of load_config: the catalog of models, environ (the shell environment over a trusted project's .env; where keys are read from), the trusted project (None: there is none), home (TAU_HOME), and the user config: the layers read again after τ writes the user's file (Driver(user_config=)).

docs.title: ModelCatalog
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModelCatalog
    models: Mapping[str, ResolvedModel]
    default_model: str | None
    warnings: tuple[ConfigProblem, ...]
    extensions: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, object]] = field(default_factory=lambda: {})
    extension_sources: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=lambda: {})
    load: Mapping[str, bool] = field(default_factory=lambda: {})
    load_sources: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=lambda: {})
    system_prompt: str | None = None
    system_prompt_source: str | None = None
    tui: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=lambda: {})

Every model the merged layers define, plus default_model, any warnings, and the extensions options the layers set ({"step_limit": {"limit": 10}}, merged per option; D16 section 4). Which options an extension has is its own to say (check_config). load is the merged top-level load (source key to on or off; D19 section 3) and load_sources the layer (file path) that set each key: what the extension loader reads. extension_sources the layer that set each extension's options (NAME) and each option (NAME.FIELD), for the problems found in them. system_prompt is the merged top-level key of that name (D20: the nearest layer's base text; None: no layer sets one, so the built-in text is used) and system_prompt_source the layer that set it (CLI for --system-prompt). tui is the merged tui object (D23: theme; only the user's file and the command line set it, a project's is an error).

docs.text:
def names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]

All qualified names, in file order.

docs.title: ModelCatalog.find
docs.text:
def find(self, name: str) -> tuple[str, ...]

Qualified names matching name. A name with : is an exact qualified name; one without is a bare search over last segments (top-level y and g:y both match y). The caller decides on 0, 1, or many.

The model named exactly qualified; ConfigError if there is none.

The layer and group each value of qualified came from.

docs.title: ModelConfig
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModelConfig
    model: str
    base_url: str | None = None
    api_key_env: str | None = None
    provider: str = 'openai'
    literal_api_key: str | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
    max_tokens: int | None = None
    options: Mapping[str, object] = field(default_factory=lambda: {})
    context_window: int | None = None
    price: Price | None = None

A resolved model: which model to ask, where (base_url, optional: a provider that needs one says so in its check), the name of the variable holding its API key, max_tokens (optional, positive), and options: a JSON object only the named provider reads, which the config loader never looks inside (D15). context_window (optional, positive) is the model's context size in tokens and price (optional) what it costs: extensions read them (D24); no provider does. The driver builds it from the catalog at each sample; no node holds it.

The key itself is never a field: it is read from the environment at sample time (api_key) and so never reaches a node or the log.

docs.title: ModelConfig.api_key
docs.text:
def api_key(self, environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> str | None

The key in environ named by api_key_env; None if no variable is named.

A literal api_key from a config file wins. Raises ConfigError if a variable is named and is unset or empty, or if the key has a character outside visible ASCII (it could not travel in an HTTP header). The error never holds the key.

class Origin

    source: str
    group: str | None

docs.title: Pick
docs.text:

A choice put to the person: takes the qualified model names, returns one of them.

docs.title: Price
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Price
    input: Decimal
    output: Decimal
    cache_read: Decimal
    cache_write: Decimal

What a model costs, in USD per million tokens: input (prompt tokens neither read from nor written to the cache), output, cache_read and cache_write. All four are required: a model that writes no cache repeats its input price for cache_write (D24 ruling 6). Amounts are Decimal, so a total of many replies has no float drift. ConfigError for a number below 0, or one that is not a number.

docs.title: Price.of
docs.text:
@classmethod

The price a config's price object says. ConfigError unless it is an object with exactly the four fields, each a number of at least 0.

Whether a source's extensions are loaded: always (tau and session_name), on, off, shadowed by another source, failed, or untrusted.

class TrustError(PermissionError)

A project directory tau cannot or will not trust, with the reason. where is the path the refusal is about (None: the project as a whole).

docs.title: Trusted
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Trusted
    root: Path
    config_text: str | None
    env_text: str | None
    extension_files: Mapping[str, bytes] | None
    system_md: bytes | None
    prompt_files: Mapping[str, bytes]

A trusted project: its root, and the exact .tau/config.json and .env text that was approved (None: no such file). extension_files is every file under .tau/extensions/ as approved (path relative to it, with /, to bytes; None: there is no such directory), which the extension loader imports from and never re-reads; system_md the bytes of .tau/SYSTEM.md as approved (None: no such file), which the prompt's assembly reads. prompt_files are the approved prompts/NAME.md and skills/NAME/SKILL.md (path relative to .tau/, with /, to bytes), which the skills extension reads. Use layer(), read_models() and project_environment rather than re-reading the files.

The project config layer for read_models, or None if there is no file.

docs.text:
def read_models(
    self,
    user: Path | LayerText | None = None,
    cli: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
) -> ModelCatalog

read_models(user, <the approved project config>, cli): the project layer is the text that was approved, not whatever the file says now.

docs.title: UntrustedProject
docs.text:
class UntrustedProject(TrustError)

The project is not trusted (or its config or .env changed). The message says what it sets and what is wrong with .tau/, and the command that trusts it unless it has errors to fix first; layer is the config it holds (None: no file), for showing its problems.

docs.title: UntrustedProject.init
docs.text: def __init__(self, root: Path, message: str, layer: LayerText | None) -> None

docs.title: UserConfig
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UserConfig
    home: Path
    project: LayerText | None = None
    cli: Mapping[str, object] | None = None

The layers a frontend loaded: the user's file under home (TAU_HOME), the approved project layer over it and the cli overrides over that, as load_config read them.

save_options writes the user layer and reads all three again, so the catalog it returns is what load_config would return now. The file is what every session reads; a Config node is one branch's.

docs.title: UserConfig.save_options
docs.text:
def save_options(
    self,
    changes: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, object]],
    check: Callable[[ModelCatalog], None],
) -> ModelCatalog

Set extensions.<name>.<field> in the user's file for each field of changes (extension, then field, to JSON value); the file's other content stays. check is given the catalog the layers make with the change, before anything is written, and raises ConfigError for options it refuses. Writes atomically, creating the file (and home, private) if absent; a symlink is followed, so the file it names is replaced and the link stays (a dangling one is a ConfigError naming it). Returns the catalog; nothing is written if any step raised. The read-change-write has no await, so on the event loop calls do not interleave; it is not safe against another τ process saving at once, or sync commands saving at once from worker threads (the last write wins). ConfigError for a file or a result the loader refuses, TrustError for a disk that refuses.

docs.title: UserConfig.save_load
docs.text:
def save_load(self, key: str, on: bool) -> ModelCatalog

Set load.<key> to on in the user's file (D19 section 3; tau ext enable and disable): whether the extension source key is loaded at start. The file's other content stays; it is written as save_options writes: atomically, a symlink followed, nothing written if a step raised. Returns the catalog the layers make now, whose load shows whether a nearer layer overrules the value. This does not know the sources: whether key names one is for the caller. ConfigError for a file the loader refuses, TrustError for a disk that refuses.

docs.title: UserConfig.save_theme
docs.text:
def save_theme(self, name: str) -> None

Set tui.theme to name in the user's file (D23 ruling 3): the theme every later tau opens in, unless --theme says otherwise for one run. The file's other content stays; it is written as save_options writes: atomically, a symlink followed, nothing written if a step raised. This does not know the themes: whether name is one is for the caller. ConfigError for a file the loader refuses, TrustError for a disk that refuses.

docs.title: UserConfig.saved
docs.text:
def saved(self, extension: str) -> dict[str, object]

extensions.<extension> as the user's file itself holds it: the fields it sets, as JSON values, and none of the project's, the overrides' or a node's ({} if the file sets none, or there is no file). ConfigError for a file the loader refuses.

docs.title: check_config
docs.text:
def check_config(
    user: Layer | None = None,
    project: Layer | None = None,
    cli: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
    environ: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    *,
    providers: Mapping[str, Provider],
    extensions: Sequence[object] = (),
) -> tuple[ConfigProblem, ...]

Every problem in the layers, not just the first. Layers: user < project < cli.

providers is the driver's map of name to provider: a model may name exactly those, and each provider's check(model) problems for the models naming it are added (D15).

extensions are those a program loads: an option the layers set for one that its options type does not have, one that does not fit, or a required one nobody set is a problem. Options for an extension not given are not looked at (it may be loaded elsewhere).

With environ, a model whose api_key_env names an unset variable is a warning. An empty result means the layers are sound.

docs.title: list_extensions
docs.text:
def list_extensions(
    cwd: Path,
    environ: Mapping[str, str],
    *,
    explicit: Sequence[str] = (),
    discover: bool = True,
) -> list[ExtensionSource]

One ExtensionSource per source in load order, tau and session_name first: what a start in cwd would import (it imports the same, and shows a failure as a row instead of raising it). It never asks about trust: a project that is not trusted shows its sources as untrusted. ConfigError or TrustError for config or trust files the loader refuses.

docs.title: load_config
docs.text:
def load_config(
    cwd: Path,
    environ: Mapping[str, str],
    *,
    ask: Ask | None,
    cli: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
) -> LoadedConfig

The layers for a frontend started in cwd: user config, the project's if trusted, then cli overrides.

ask is the live terminal's approval question (prompts(...).ask); without one an untrusted project raises UntrustedProject. ConfigError and TrustError propagate unchanged. The returned environ is environ over the trusted project's .env.

docs.title: load_extensions
docs.text:
def load_extensions(
    loaded: LoadedConfig,
    *,
    explicit: Sequence[str] = (),
    discover: bool = True,
) -> list[Extension]

The extensions to run, in hook order (the driver puts tau first; a program adds session_name, D18, after this returns).

The sources are the built-ins that load leaves on and, with discover, the installed packages and the user's and the trusted project's drop-ins that it leaves on; then explicit (-e values: paths, or the keys of sources, discovered or built-in, which load whatever load says; relative paths are taken against the working directory, see absolute_explicit). Without discover (--no-extensions) the packages and drop-ins are skipped, explicit still loads, and the built-ins (base_tools, step_limit) stay as load says. base_tools is built when this runs and roots its tools at the process's working directory then, so a program that calls this must change directory first, as start_session does. ExtensionLoadError naming every source that failed, with the one command that gets past each: nothing is started or written by then.

docs.title: model_config
docs.text:
def model_config(
    model: str | None = None,
    extensions: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, object]] | None = None,
) -> Config

The Config node body that sets model (a catalog's qualified name; it holds that name and nothing resolved from the file) and/or the options in extensions ({"step_limit": {"limit": 10}}), from this node on, and nothing else. ConfigError if it sets neither.

The Prompts for these streams.

    user: Layer | None = None,

Merge the layers (user < project < cli; each may be absent) and resolve.

docs.title: select_model
docs.text:
def select_model(catalog: ModelCatalog, requested: str | None = None, *, pick: Pick | None) -> str

The qualified name to use: requested (--model), else the catalog's default_model.

A name with : must be exactly a qualified name. A bare name with one match is that match; with several, pick (a live terminal) chooses among the qualified names and without one ConfigError lists them. No match is a ConfigError with close names.

docs.text:
def system_prompt(
    cwd: Path,
    loaded: LoadedConfig,
    *,
    append: Sequence[str] = (),
    context_files: bool = True,

The prompt for a session in cwd (resolved here), given the loaded config: its base text, append (--append-system-prompt, in order) and, if context_files, the files as the module says. A part with no text is left out. ContextFileError for a file found and unusable.

docs.title: Driver
docs.text:
class Driver

Runs one session's cursors over providers, tools, and extensions.

providers maps each provider name to the provider a model with that provider is sampled by; each must be named by its own name. The program that built them closes them. catalog is where a Config node's model name is resolved, at each sample. user_config (LoadedConfig.user) is what lets an extension save its options to the user's file (Cursor.save_options, /config --save); without it they raise ConfigError.

A frontend never calls the driver: it holds a Client (client(id) makes one, naming itself), whose calls run on the loop thread, publish what they changed, and poke the pump. Once the driver has failed or stopped they raise ConnectionError (the failure's "Type: msg", chained, or "the driver is stopped"), as rest does; a stream connected then ends at once. The extensions' commands (/model of the built-in extension tau first) run for clients; a command that takes a Cursor runs ahead of the pre_step hooks of a step the driver asks for. Aborting or going elsewhere cancels it. Extensions are listed in the constructor, in hook order, and checked there like tools (DefinitionError); model.md does not yet say how config_at names them. reload swaps them for others while nothing is in flight.

docs.text:

    session: Session,
    providers: Mapping[str, Provider],
    catalog: ModelCatalog,
    *,
    tools: Sequence[Tool | Callable[..., object]] = (),
    extensions: Sequence[Extension] = (),
    clock: Clock | None = None,

docs.title: Driver.reload
docs.text:
def reload(self, extensions: Sequence[Extension]) -> None

Run extensions (listed in hook order, as at construction) instead of the ones the driver has, with the same tools: rebuild the options, tools, tool owners and commands, and forget every folded Config. Only when nothing is in flight: no cursor busy (a command waiting for its step has none out yet, but its cursor is busy) and no effect out, since every job holds the set it was dispatched with (Busy naming the cursors); the next job dispatched uses the new one. DefinitionError (nothing changes) as at construction. The tree is not rewritten: a Config node that sets options of an extension no longer here (or no longer fitting its type) fails when it is read (ConfigError), not now. Clients are told nothing, as after use_catalog: they ask commands() and options() again.

docs.text:
def start(self) -> None

Start the pump. Call inside the running loop.

docs.title: Driver.stop
docs.text:
async def stop(self) -> None

Cancel everything without answering, as a crash would. rest and every frontend call raise from now on; client streams end, later ones at once.

docs.title: Driver.rest
docs.text:
async def rest(self, cursor: int, waiter: int | None = None) -> None

Wait until the cursor is at rest with no effect out. Raises ConnectionError once the driver has failed or stopped (also if it does meanwhile). A cursor held by an open question or a gate does not rest. Returns early if waiter, the cursor that waits (a handle's), is aborted or left meanwhile.

docs.text:

A client named id (stable across reconnects: john@laptop:tui), connected now, its stream opening with the snapshot: make it inside the running loop. buffer bounds the stream (Feed).

docs.title: Driver.add_item
docs.text:
def add_item(self, to: int, data: ItemData) -> int

Add an item to a cursor's scratchpad; the cursor wakes. For whoever has something to tell a resting cursor from outside a hook: a timer extension, tau serve relaying a webhook. An ItemData.Input is what a client's input and send add (they say who typed it), so it is refused here. A hook adds its extension's item with its handle's add_item.

docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DriverState
    units: int
    queued: bool
    open_questions: int
    parked: int
    failure: Exception | None
    stopped: bool

What a harness reads to tell quiet from busy: the effects running (units), whether the pump has something to do (queued: a report or poke to take, or a busy cursor with no effect out; never once the driver has failed or stopped, when the session may be closed), the questions open, the effects parked in the driver (parked: an effect with a question open or a handle's rest or close_cursor out waits for an answer or another cursor, and counts once however many it has out), what the driver died of, and whether it was stopped. check raises ConnectionError for a failed or stopped driver, as every client call does first.

docs.title: CursorGone
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CursorGone
    cursor: int
    at: int

Cursor cursor is closed (D17): a client drops its view of it. at is the node it was last at, for restarting (reopen). A cursor has one state event at a time: its CursorView while open, this after it closes. Labels may still name it: they are its restart record.

docs.title: CursorView
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CursorView
    cursor: int
    at: int
    busy: bool
    auto: bool
    questions: tuple[OpenQuestion, ...]
    items: tuple[Item, ...]
    ending: Ending | None
    hook_error: HookFailure | None
    model: str | None
    shown: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]

One cursor as a client sees it, whole: where it is (at), whether a step is running (busy), auto-step, its open questions (oldest first), its pending items (an ItemData.Input says who wrote it: its by), and how its last step ended (ending) with the hook_error that ended it, if a cursor hook failed in it. Both are None from the start of a step until it ends, and after a reload. model is the qualified name of the model the cursor's branch is on (what its next sample uses), None if no Config on the branch names one or one is unreadable (a sample says which). shown is what each extension shows on the cursor (Cursor.show), as (extension, text) pairs in extension-name order; it is not in the log, so it is empty after a reload.

A provider is waiting to try the sample again (D24 section 4): this is retry attempt of attempts, after seconds, because the last try failed with reason. It is no part of the reply and is never replayed to a client that starts watching later: it says what the sample is doing now, and the next delta (or the end of the sample) replaces it.

docs.text:

    call_id: str

A running call showing partial output: text is new output since the last ToolProgress of the same call, not the whole so far. The call is named by node, the batch's node (the Assistant node holding the call), and call_id: a server may reuse ids across batches, so the id alone does not say which call. Only the driver makes one (a tool calls its progress); a provider cannot yield one. What the call saves is its Outcome, never this.

docs.title: Cursor
docs.text:
class Cursor(TreeHandle)

What a cursor hook acts through: one cursor, bound to its extension.

The tree handle, plus the cursor's own move, write, and set_auto, which core allows only while a cursor hook job is out for the cursor. Once the hook coroutine returns (retire), they raise NotInHook; so does every other write and ask. Reads still work. Core checks no more than that the tree stays valid (no hook edit limits).

docs.title: Cursor.show
docs.text:
def show(self, text: str | None) -> None

Show text on this cursor to every client, as this extension's one line (CursorView.shown); a later call replaces it, and None shows nothing. It is not in the log or the scratchpad: it is gone when the session is reloaded, and dropped when the cursor closes. TypeError for anything else.

docs.title: Cursor.set_model
docs.text:
def set_model(self, model: Model) -> int

Write a Config node under at that sets the branch's model (a qualified name) and move onto it, as write does. ConfigError if it is not configured; nothing is written then. Returns the new node's id.

docs.title: Cursor.set_options
docs.text:
def set_options(self, **changes: object) -> int

Write a Config node under at that sets these options of this extension (JSON values) and move onto it, as write does: each replaces the walk's earlier value. ConfigError if the extension has no options, or those that result, folded with the walk's, do not fit its options type (a __post_init__ that raises refuses); nothing is written then. Returns the new node's id.

docs.title: Cursor.save_options
docs.text:
def save_options(self, **changes: object) -> None

Write these options of this extension (JSON values) into the user's config file, extensions.<name> in <TAU_HOME>/config.json, and have the driver read it at once. The file is every session's and every branch's; set_options is this branch's, a node. No node is written and nothing moves. The project's config is never written. ConfigError if the extension has no options, the options that result (the layers, with these) do not fit its options type, or the driver was given no user config; nothing is written then.

The file is read, changed and written back with no await in between, so on the event loop (a hook, a tool, an async command) saves cannot interleave. It is not safe against another τ process saving at the same moment (the last write wins, losing the other's change), nor from sync commands that save at once on worker threads.

docs.title: Cursor.saved_options
docs.text:
def saved_options(self) -> Mapping[str, object]

What the user's config file itself sets of this extension's options, as JSON values ({} if it sets none, or there is no file): the value save_options changes, not options(), which folds the project's layer, the overrides and this branch's nodes in. To add to a list option in the file, read it here, not there. ConfigError if the extension has no options or the driver was given no user config.

def tell(self, text: str, *, to: str | None = None) -> None

Send text as a Notice to client to, or to every connected client by default. Dropped if to is not connected: a notice is for someone who is there.

docs.title: Cursor.ask
docs.text:
async def ask(self, text: str, expect: object = str, *, to: str | None = None) -> Any

Ask the cursor's clients text, and wait for an answer of type expect (any hint of the type language; str by default). Returns the checked, converted answer, or None if declined. to names the client asked first (None: anyone; a client that is not connected is the same). The hook's job stays out meanwhile, however long and whoever is connected, so the cursor is busy; an abort or go-to declines it (and any asked later in that step). A CursorId answer of "new" opens a cursor at the cursor's at.

docs.title: Extension
docs.text:
class Extension(Protocol)

Hooks are methods named for their hook point, found by name and all optional.

Cursor hooks (CursorHook): pre_step, pre_input, pre_sample, pre_reply, post_reply, post_result, post_step. Tool hooks (ToolHook): pre_tool, pre_result. name is non-empty and unique among a driver's extensions; any attribute named pre_* or post_* that is not a hook point is refused when the driver is built (DefinitionError), so a misspelt hook cannot sit silent. That covers data too: a dataclass field pre_prompt is refused. Name such a field for what it holds (prompt_prefix, before_prompt), never with those two prefixes.

Optional attributes besides the hooks: tools, commands, options, yields_names, and rescan (Rescanning).

docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RequestCount
    total: Count
    base: Count
    base_nodes: int
    nodes: Mapping[int, Count]
    why: str | None = None

What the walk to a node will cost as a request (Cursor.count).

total is the whole request. base counts the walk's first base_nodes nodes and the request's overhead (tool definitions, hidden prompts, per-message overhead) as one; it is NONE with base_nodes 0 while no reply on the walk has reported its usage. nodes has one count for each node that is sent, by node id, except a node inside a lump: where two requests prove that the nodes between them cost a known sum, the first node holds the sum and the others have no count of their own, so a cut never lands inside one. why says why the total is weaker than it could be, or is None.

docs.title: StepLimit
docs.text:
class StepLimit
    name = 'step_limit'
    options = Options

Turns a cursor's auto-step off after limit unattended steps in a row (D1).

The limit is the extension's option (Options.limit, 50 unless configured), read at each hook, so /config step_limit changes it for a branch.

It guards the loops where the cursor does move every step, such as a model that calls tools forever or a hook that writes "continue" after every reply. A cursor that does not move is stopped by core, not by this limit.

The count is this object's own memory, per cursor, kept at hook points:

  • pre_input sets it to 1: the step that takes an input is the first. There is no post_input hook; pre_input fires once per input item offered.
  • pre_step adds one, when the cursor's auto-step is on. A step run with auto-step off (a frontend's step, a load) is attended and is not counted.
  • post_step turns auto-step off when the count has reached limit, and starts the count over, so whoever resumes the cursor (set_auto) gets another limit steps. It also starts over whenever it sees auto-step off: a halt, an abort, or a go-to ended the run.

When core turns auto-step off because a step did not move the cursor, that happens after post_step: the count stays as it was until the next input.

A hook that leaves an input pending offers it again every step, so pre_input restarts the count every time: this limit does not bound that. List it after any extension that turns auto-step back on from post_step, or that hook's set_auto(True) wins.

docs.title: TreeHandle.rest
docs.text:
async def rest(self, cursor: int) -> Ending | None

Wait until cursor is at rest with no effect out, and return how its last step ended; None if that is not known (it has not stepped since the session was loaded). After a send to a cursor that was at rest, this is the ending of the step the send caused. If the cursor was mid-step, the input waits for that step to end and this may return that earlier step's ending with the input still pending: to wait for the step a send causes, rest first, then send, then rest again. A cursor held by an open question or a gate does not rest, so this waits as long as the cursor is held. Async only: a sync tool, which runs on a worker thread, cannot call it. ValueError for this handle's own cursor: waiting for itself would never end. No cycle between two cursors is detected; the user's abort is the way out: when this handle's own cursor is aborted (or sent elsewhere) while the wait is out, the wait ends at once and returns Ending.Aborted(), so a hook, which an abort never cancels, learns it was aborted. The cursor waited on is left as it is.

docs.title: TreeHandle.abort
docs.text:
def abort(self, cursor: int) -> None

Abort cursor's step as a client's abort does: cancel its sample or calls, stop its command, decline its open questions, and turn its auto-step off. Safe from a sync tool's worker thread: it returns once the event loop has done it. ValueError for this handle's own cursor: aborting it would cancel this very call.

docs.title: TreeHandle.close_cursor
docs.text:
async def close_cursor(self, cursor: int) -> None

Close cursor: abort its step as abort does, wait for it to rest, drop its pending items, and close it (D17). It leaves cursors() and the clients' views; its id, its last node (in closed()) and its labels stay, which is what reopen restarts from. Anyone waiting on it sees the abort. CursorClosed if it is already closed. Async only, like rest. ValueError for this handle's own cursor: closing it would wait on itself.

docs.title: TreeHandle.reopen
docs.text:
def reopen(self, cursor: int) -> int

Open a new cursor at the closed cursor's last node and move each of its labels onto it, as this extension. Returns the new id. ValueError if cursor is open, NoSuchCursor if it was never opened.

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
class Session

One session: its tree, cursors, scratchpad, and every cursor's step. It does no IO of its own: a program asks it for each cursor's next Job and gives back an Answer.

A call that changes the session hands its records to the store (when there is one) before it returns, so a program never saves. Every call takes the session's one lock, so a session may be shared across threads. A closed session raises Closed.

docs.title: AnthropicProvider
docs.text:
class AnthropicProvider

Samples the Anthropic Messages API (/v1/messages) for the ModelConfig the driver resolved. base_url is the API's root, https://api.anthropic.com when unset (a proxy that speaks the same API may be named; give no /v1).

One client serves every sample (see Connection). transport replaces the network (a test's httpx.MockTransport); environ is where api_key_env is looked up, at sample time.

check requires a key (api_key_env) and max_tokens (the API requires it; there is no default), and reads the options in _OPTIONS, refusing any other: thinking (an object as the API takes it: type a string, budget_tokens for enabled, display; the API judges the values, and check refuses only what needs a beta header this provider cannot send), effort (a string, sent as output_config.effort), temperature, top_p (numbers), top_k (an integer), prompt_caching (a boolean, default true: mark the system text and the last message for caching), and extra_body (an object merged into the request body last; it may not set model, messages, system, stream, tools, max_tokens, thinking, or a key the model's settings set).

docs.title: GeminiProvider
docs.text:
class GeminiProvider

Samples Gemini's streamGenerateContent (?alt=sse) for the ModelConfig the driver resolved.

One client serves every sample (see Connection). transport replaces the network (a test's httpx.MockTransport); environ is where api_key_env is looked up, at sample time.

Settings: base_url defaults to the official endpoint; a proxy sets it. A key is required (api_key_env or api_key) and goes in the x-goog-api-key header. max_tokens is maxOutputTokens, which Gemini counts thinking into. Options (check refuses any other): temperature, top_p, top_k (numbers); thinking, an object of include_thoughts (bool: ask for thought summaries, which arrive as Thinking; without it none are requested), budget (integer, -1 dynamic, 0 off: Gemini 2.5) or level (a string: Gemini 3), not both; safety_settings, a list of {category, threshold} passed through, one per category; and extra_body, an object merged into the request last, for what the API has that these do not (it may not set contents, systemInstruction or tools, nor a key the model's settings set; its generationConfig merges into ours).

docs.title: Provider.sample
docs.text:
def sample(
    self,
    walk: Sequence[Node],
    model: ModelConfig,
    tools: Sequence['Tool'],
) -> AsyncGenerator[Part | Finish | Delta, None]

model is the session's named model, resolved by the driver at this sample. Yield, interleaved: deltas as text arrives (TextDelta, ThinkingDelta, CallNamed then CallArgs), each whole part as it finishes, then the Finish, then end. The driver saves only the parts and forwards the deltas. A part is yielded before the first delta of the next part; a delta that breaks this fails the sample. tools are the driver's, offered to the model for this sample only; they are never recorded.

sample assumes check(model) returned no problems: the driver calls it first, for every sample, and fails the sample with the problems listed if it returns any, so sample does not re-check. It closes the generator when it stops reading.

Raise SampleError to fail; parts yielded before it are kept. Any other Exception (from check or from sample) fails this sample the same way, with its message as Type: message and internal: true in meta.error, and its traceback on stderr: a bug in a provider costs one sample, never the driver. If the sample is cancelled or fails, the driver saves the text or thinking whose deltas arrived but whose part never did. A part yielded while deltas are open must be the part those deltas were building (same kind, same text), and Finish may not come with deltas open.

def replay_for(part: Part, provider: str) -> dict[str, object] | None

The replay data provider may send back for part, parsed: the JSON object in part.replay.data when the part carries replay tagged with provider; None for a part with none, or with another provider's, which the caller treats as unsigned (model.md 10.4). def extension_flags() -> argparse.ArgumentParser

A parser (add_help=False, for parents=) with the flags that choose extensions: -e VALUE (repeatable; a path, or the key of a source: a discovered one or a built-in) and --no-extensions. tau.start_session reads them from the parsed args.

docs.title: tau.cli.main
docs.text:
def main(
    argv: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    *,
    stdin: TextIO | None = None,
    stdout: TextIO | None = None,
    stderr: TextIO | None = None,
    environ: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    cwd: Path | None = None,
) -> int

Run tau with argv (default sys.argv[1:]); the other arguments default to the process's streams, environment, and working directory. Returns the exit status.

The process's streams may be missing or go away, as any Unix program's may. A closed standard input (<&-) reads as empty; a closed standard error says nothing; a closed standard output is an error (status 1, said on standard error); and a standard output whose reader has gone (tau -p ... | head -1) ends the run quietly with status 141, 128 plus SIGPIPE, as a program killed by that signal would.

A parser (add_help=False, for parents=) with the flags that choose the session (D18 section 5): -c/--continue, -r/--resume, --session REF, --fork REF and --no-session (at most one), -n/--name NAME and --session-dir DIR; and the prompt flags of a new session (D20): --system-prompt TEXT, --append-system-prompt TEXT (repeatable) and -nc/--no-context-files. The session session names, tried in this order: a path (it contains /), an id, an exact name, a unique id prefix. The whole of sessions is searched. A name or prefix of several sessions, or of none, is UnknownSession. With first, the row also has first.

docs.title: list_sessions
docs.text:
def list_sessions(sessions: Path, *, cwd: Path | None = None) -> list[SessionInfo]

The rows of sessions, newest updated first; those whose cwd equals cwd (resolved) exactly, or all with cwd=None. A directory that is not a readable session is a row with an error and is listed either way. Reads info.json and stats log per session, and the start of the log of a session with no name (its first). Anything that is not a directory is ignored.

docs.title: open_client
docs.text:
async def open_client(
    args: object,
    *,
    client: str,
    environ: Mapping[str, str],
    cwd: Path,
    system: SystemText | None = None,
    prompts: Prompts | None = None,
    pick_session: PickSession | None = None,
    own: Sequence[Extension] = (),
    model: str | None = None,
    clock: Clock | None = None,
) -> Opened

Open the session args choose (see start_session for the arguments and what it raises) and a client named client of it, as the module says: attached to the tau serve that holds it, else started here. ConfigError when attached and -e, --no-extensions, --set, -n, own or --model ask for what the server's loaded session cannot take; Leased for a session another process holds that is no server; LookupError for a session with no cursor. Close the result with Opened.close.

docs.title: rename_session
docs.text:
def rename_session(path: Path, name: str) -> None

Give the session in path the name name (stripped); an empty name removes it. No lease is taken: the file is replaced whole, and the last of two renames wins. ConfigError for a name with a / or a : in it (a ref could not name the session by it), ValueError if info.json is not readable.

docs.title: start_session
docs.text:
async def start_session(
    args: object,
    *,
    environ: Mapping[str, str],
    cwd: Path,
    system: SystemText | None = None,
    prompts: Prompts | None = None,
    pick_session: PickSession | None = None,
    own: Sequence[Extension] = (),
    model: str | None = None,
    clock: Clock | None = None,
) -> Started

Start the session args (the parsed session_flags() and extension_flags()) choose, for a program started in cwd with environ, as the module says. own are the program's own extensions, ahead of the loaded ones; model is --model; prompts ask a person to trust a project or to pick a model; pick_session is what -r asks; system is the text of a new session's System node (default: D20's tau.system_prompt, from the prompt flags in args).

Raises what the steps raise: ConfigError, TrustError, ExtensionLoadError, UnknownSession, Leased, FileNotFoundError for a session whose working directory is gone. Nothing is created when a step before the session's fails, and a session this call created is removed if a later step fails.

docs.title: BashTool
docs.text:
class BashTool

bash: a shell command with a timeout. Keeps the tail of long output.

timeout_ms is the timeout of a call that gives none, max_timeout_ms the most a call may ask for (more is an Err), kill_grace_ms the time between SIGTERM and SIGKILL. Cancelling call terminates the command's whole process group and waits for it to end before the CancelledError propagates, however often it is cancelled meanwhile: no child is left running. Each call has a thread of its own.

docs.title: BashTool.call
docs.text:
async def call(self, args_raw: str, *, progress: Progress | None = None) -> Outcome

Run the command. With progress, the output also goes to it as it arrives: at most one call per 100 ms, carrying all the text since the last, from a thread of the engine's own. The answer is the same either way. The command never waits on progress: a slow one loses the oldest output it has not yet been given (the answer keeps its 10 kB and the overflow file all of it). The answer does wait for a progress call already running and for the final flush, one more call, so a slow progress delays the answer by that much. Calls stop for good when the interpreter begins to exit.

What the driver and providers depend on. A plain function is described as one (tau._tools); any object with these attributes works too.

Any object with these attributes works, whatever it is written in. The tool owns argument validation: it gets the call's raw JSON text.

A tool that shows partial output as it runs opts in by giving call a parameter named progress (call(self, args_raw, *, progress=None); the None default keeps the tool a Tool and callable without a driver), detected once when the driver is built. class TauApp(App[None])
    CSS_PATH = 'tau.tcss'
    COMMANDS: ClassVar[set[type[Provider] | Callable[[], type[Provider]]]] = {TauCommands}
    BINDINGS: ClassVar[list[BindingType]] = [Binding('escape', 'abort', 'Abort', show=False), Binding('ctrl+c', 'interrupt', 'Abort / quit', show=False, priority=True), Binding('ctrl+q', 'quit', 'Quit', show=False, priority=True), Binding('ctrl+r', "fold('thinking')", 'Fold thinking', show=False), Binding('ctrl+t', "fold('tools')", 'Fold tool boxes', show=False), Binding('alt+left', "move('previous')", 'Previous cursor', show=False), Binding('alt+right', "move('next')", 'Next cursor', show=False), Binding('ctrl+g', "move('tree')", 'The tree', show=False), Binding('ctrl+o', "move('sessions')", 'Sessions', show=False), Binding('ctrl+n', "move('new')", 'New session', show=False), Binding('ctrl+up', "scroll('up')", 'Scroll up', show=False), Binding('ctrl+down', "scroll('down')", 'Scroll down', show=False)]

The terminal UI of one session, over client, viewing cursor.

welcome is the server's (or the local start's) answer: the session id and working directory the header shows (None for a session kept in memory, whose header shows cwd, the directory it works in). snapshot are the events the client's stream already gave up (Opened.snapshot); a client whose stream has not been read needs none. theme names one of the themes (None: the default); user themes are read from home, which is TAU_HOME. reconnect, for a remote client, makes a new client with the same id; without it a stream that ends in ConnectionError ends the app's session: the failure is shown, the transcript stays readable and return_code is 1 once the person quits.

The keys: Enter sends, Ctrl+J starts a new line, Tab completes, Esc aborts the cursor's step (or declines the question the keyboard is in), Ctrl+C aborts if busy, else clears the draft, else quits when pressed twice, Ctrl+R folds the thinking and Ctrl+T the tool boxes, Ctrl+Q quits. / starts a command; one missing arguments opens a form for them.

A centred modal with a title, a body, and escape meaning cancel.

Subclasses supply :meth:compose_body and, usually, :attr:TITLE_TEXT. What they do NOT supply is the shell, the centering, the title styling or the cancel binding — those are the things every dialog agreed on by accident before, and the things a new dialog now gets without asking.

Attributes: DIALOG_ID: The shell's widget id. Carries the two properties that genuinely differ between dialogs (width, height); everything else comes from the tau-dialog class. TITLE_TEXT: The title, for a dialog whose title never varies. A dialog whose title is supplied per instance passes it to __init__ instead. CANCEL_VALUE: What escape dismisses with. None for a dialog returning an optional value, False for a confirmation — a cancelled question is never a hidden yes. BODY_ID: Set it to give the dialog a scrolling body with that id between a header (the title plus :meth:compose_header) and a footer (:meth:compose_footer), both pinned, so the buttons stay on screen however long the body is . None keeps the plain stack.
