docs.title: Tau 0.16 preview API: The wire protocol
docs.text:
Unreleased

Generated from the docstrings of Tau 0.16.0-dev (commit c439c401) by scripts/api_docs.py in the Tau repository. Not the 0.15 API.

docs.title: The wire protocol
docs.text: tau serve serves one session over a Unix socket, so a frontend in any language can drive it. Python programs use RemoteClient and need none of this page; it is for the author of a client in another language. For what the calls mean, read the model and writing a frontend: the wire is the Client contract, serialized.

docs.title: How it travels
docs.text:
• Transport. A WebSocket over the Unix socket $TAU_HOME/serve/<session id>.sock (or the --socket path). The socket's file permissions are the only authentication. tau serve -d --json prints the socket's path; see the quickstart.
  • Messages. JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per WebSocket text message. A client sends requests, with parameters by name only ({"cursor": 0, "text": "hi"}). It sends no batches and no notifications. The server answers each request, and sends the notifications event and end.
  • hello comes first. It names the protocol the client speaks, the client's stable id (john@laptop:vscode) and, if it wants one, the buffer of its event stream. The answer is a Welcome. A different protocol number is refused with ProtocolMismatch and the connection closes: the match is exact. Any other request before hello, or a second hello, is an invalid request and closes the connection.
  • One call per Client method. The method has the Client method's name, and a call that returns nothing answers null. Calls begin in the order they arrive and may finish in any order; match a response to its request by id. close is not a call: close the connection.
  • Events. The notification event has the event's fields as its parameters, plus kind, the event's name ({"kind": "CursorView", "cursor": 0, ...}). The server sends every event a response depends on before the response: when open answers 3, the CursorView of cursor 3 has already arrived. A client hears Live events only for the cursors it watches; every other event goes to every client.
  • The end. The last message is the notification end, then the server closes the connection. Its error is null when the server stopped, CutOff when the client fell too far behind its buffer, and Stopped when the driver failed.
  • No resume. A reconnecting client gets a fresh snapshot of events and reads the tree again. The log is the truth.

docs.title: Reading a value
docs.text:
Two styles share the schema, and both are tagged the way Rust's serde tags them:

  • A node and what it holds (Body, Part, Outcome, Author, Item, Ending) are externally tagged: a variant with data is an object with one key, {"User": "hi"}, and a variant without is a bare string, "Core". This is the encoding of the session's own log.
  • An event carries its name in kind.

Everything else is plain JSON: a dataclass is an object, a tuple an array. Node ids, cursor ids and item ids are non-negative integers, dense, and never reused. A node never changes once written, so a client may cache it.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
A failed call answers a JSON-RPC error object: code, message (the exception's text) and, for two codes, data. The table names every code. RemoteClient raises the Python class in its last column, so a client in another language maps codes to its own errors the same way.

A call on a server whose driver has stopped or failed answers Stopped (-32013).

The descriptions below say which error a call answers by the name in the table, which gives its code. Where a value is absent they say null.

docs.title: The version
docs.text: protocol in hello is an integer, now 1. It changes only between tagged releases, when the schema below changed since the last tag. Between releases the wire changes freely: build a client against the schema of the tau you run, and check tau serve --schema.

docs.title: Calls
docs.text: Every call of Client. hello is first; the rest follow in any order.

docs.title: hello method
docs.text:
The first message of a connection: the protocol the client speaks, its stable client id (john@laptop:vscode) and the buffer of its event stream (the server's default if left out). A different protocol is ProtocolMismatch. The server answers Welcome.

Parameters:

field type notes protocol integer client string buffer integer or null optional

Result: Welcome

docs.title: abort method
docs.text:
Abort the cursor's step and decline its open questions.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer

Result: null

docs.title: answer method
docs.text:
Answer an open question with a decoded JSON value; null declines. Refused if the value is wrong (the question stays open), NotFound if the question is closed or unknown (the first good answer wins), NotYours if it is for another client.

Parameters:

field type notes question integer value any JSON value

Result: null

docs.title: children method
docs.text:
The ids of the children of node id, in append order.

Parameters:

field type notes id integer

Result: array of integer

docs.title: close_cursor method
docs.text:
Close the cursor (D17): abort its step as abort does, wait for it to rest, drop its pending items, and close it. Clients are sent a CursorGone. Its id, last node and labels stay; reopen restarts from them. CursorClosed if it is already closed.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer

Result: null

docs.title: commands method
docs.text:
Each command's form: its name, description and argument schema (named types with their "format", each default), fixed until the driver reloads. If some extension has options there is one more, config, whose one argument is the extension; it is changed with configure, not run.

No parameters.

Result: array of Form

docs.title: complete method
docs.text:
The values of a named type ("path", "model", "cursor", "label", "node"; the "format" of a schema) that start with prefix, as cursor sees them. Paths are the driver's machine's, relative to its working directory.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer named string prefix string

Result: array of string

docs.title: complete_line method
docs.text:
commandline.completions of line on the driver: what could finish its last word, in one call.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer line string

Result: array of string

docs.title: configure method
docs.text:
Change the options named in values (decoded JSON) of extension on cursor's branch: a step of the cursor writes a Config node. With save, the server also writes the user's config file (extensions.<name>), which every session reads: the options in values and those a Config node on the branch set, wherever they differ from the file's (options equal to the file's stay untouched; values may be {}; options only the user, project or command-line layers set are not copied). A client needs no access to that file. ConfigError for an extension without options, or values its options type refuses (or, with save, a driver with no user config), Busy unless the cursor is at rest; nothing is written then, neither node nor file.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer extension string values object save boolean optional

Result: null

docs.title: go_to method
docs.text:
Move the cursor to node to, aborting a busy step (which declines its open questions).

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer to integer

Result: null

docs.title: input method
docs.text:
Add text to the cursor's scratchpad as this client's input; returns the item.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer text string

Result: integer

docs.title: node method
docs.text:
The node with this id; NoSuchNode if there is none.

Parameters:

field type notes id integer

Result: Node

docs.title: nodes method
docs.text:
Up to limit nodes from id start, in id order; none past the end. Ids are dense and a node never changes, so a tree is read in ranges. Refused for a negative start or limit.

Parameters:

field type notes start integer limit integer

Result: array of Node

docs.title: open method
docs.text:
Open a cursor at node at; it wakes. Returns its id.

Parameters:

field type notes at integer

Result: integer

docs.title: options method
docs.text:
extension's options as they stand at cursor: a form whose schema has every option, each default the value now. ConfigError if it has no options.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer extension string

Result: Form

docs.title: parse_line method
docs.text:
commandline.parse of line with this driver's forms and the options forms cursor sees: the command, its arguments, and the required parameters still missing. UnknownCommand if no command has the name (send the line as text), Refused for a line that cannot be read, plain NotFound for a bare name two extensions share.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer line string

Result: Parsed

docs.title: remove_item method
docs.text:
Take back a pending input this client added to cursor (input or send): it is removed from the scratchpad before the cursor delivers it. NotFound once it is delivered, or if there is no such item on the cursor; NotYours for an item another client or an extension added. Wakes nothing and does not turn auto-step off.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer item integer

Result: null

docs.title: remove_label method
docs.text:
Remove label; NoSuchLabel if there is none.

Parameters:

field type notes label string

Result: null

docs.title: reopen method
docs.text:
Open a new cursor at the closed cursor's last node, and move each of its labels onto it. Returns the new id. Refused if cursor is open, NoSuchCursor if it was never opened.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer

Result: integer

docs.title: run method
docs.text:
Run /command ("note", or "a:note", the extension's qualified name) with decoded JSON args on cursor; returns the command's result (null if it has none) once it has finished. CommandFailed (its message is the failure as "Type: msg") if it raised, or was aborted; it is raised as soon as the command raises, even when the command's step has not yet ended: the cursor may still be busy for a moment while the step ends, and a retry then gets Busy. A command's progress and cursor.tell arrive as Notices. NotFound for an unknown command or a bare name two extensions share ("/note is two commands: /a:note, /b:note"), Refused naming the problem for arguments that fit no parameter (the values are checked with the session, "new" last), Busy for a command that runs as a step of the cursor when it is not at rest.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer command string args object

Result: string or null

docs.title: send method
docs.text:
input with auto-step on.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer text string

Result: integer

docs.title: set_auto method
docs.text:
Turn cursor's auto-step on or off; on wakes it.

Parameters:

field type notes cursor integer on boolean

Result: null

docs.title: set_label method
docs.text:

field type notes cursor integer label string

docs.title: step method
docs.text:

docs.title: watch method

docs.title: Events
docs.text: The params of the notification event.

docs.title: Live
docs.text:
A delta, on the cursor whose sample or tool call produced it. Never in the tree: a client draws it as a layer over the cursor. Only a client watching the cursor hears it.

field type notes kind "Live" cursor integer delta TextDelta or ThinkingDelta or CallNamed or CallArgs or Retrying or ToolProgress

docs.title: CursorView
docs.text:
One cursor as a client sees it, whole: where it is (at), whether a step is running (busy), auto-step, its open questions (oldest first), its pending items (an ItemData.Input says who wrote it: its by), and how its last step ended (ending) with the hook_error that ended it, if a cursor hook failed in it. Both are null from the start of a step until it ends, and after a reload. model is the qualified name of the model the cursor's branch is on (what its next sample uses), null if no Config on the branch names one or one is unreadable (a sample says which). shown is what each extension shows on the cursor (Cursor.show), as (extension, text) pairs in extension-name order; it is not in the log, so it is empty after a reload.

field type notes kind "CursorView" cursor integer at integer busy boolean auto boolean questions array of OpenQuestion items array of Item ending Ending or null hook_error HookFailure or null model string or null shown array of [string, string]

docs.title: CursorGone
docs.text:
Cursor cursor is closed (D17): a client drops its view of it. at is the node it was last at, for restarting (reopen). A cursor has one state event at a time: its CursorView while open, this after it closes. Labels may still name it: they are its restart record.

field type notes kind "CursorGone" cursor integer at integer

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
Every label and the cursor it is on, in label order.

field type notes kind "Labels" labels array of [string, integer]

docs.title: Appended
docs.text:
Nodes added to the tree, in id order, bodies included.

field type notes kind "Appended" nodes array of Node

docs.title: Notice
docs.text:
A message for one client, or for all of them: cursor.tell (to every client unless it names one), or an input a hook refused (to its author).

field type notes kind "Notice" text string

docs.title: Deltas
docs.text: A Live event's delta is one of these, tagged by kind.

docs.title: TextDelta
docs.text:
Text of the reply arriving.

field type notes kind "TextDelta" text string

docs.title: ThinkingDelta
docs.text:
Thinking text arriving.

field type notes kind "ThinkingDelta" text string

docs.title: CallNamed
docs.text:
A call begins forming: call number index in this reply, with its id and tool.

field type notes kind "CallNamed" index integer id string tool string

docs.title: CallArgs
docs.text:
More of call index's argument text (args_raw).

field type notes kind "CallArgs" index integer text string

docs.title: Retrying
docs.text:
A provider is waiting to try the sample again (D24 section 4): this is retry attempt of attempts, after seconds, because the last try failed with reason. It is no part of the reply and is never replayed to a client that starts watching later: it says what the sample is doing now, and the next delta (or the end of the sample) replaces it.

field type notes kind "Retrying" attempt integer attempts integer seconds number reason string

docs.title: ToolProgress
docs.text:
A running call showing partial output: text is new output since the last ToolProgress of the same call, not the whole so far. The call is named by node, the batch's node (the Assistant node holding the call), and call_id: a server may reuse ids across batches, so the id alone does not say which call. Only the driver makes one (a tool calls its progress); a provider cannot yield one. What the call saves is its Outcome, never this.

field type notes kind "ToolProgress" node integer call_id string text string

docs.title: The end
docs.text:
The params of the last message: the notification end. error is null when the driver stopped, else CutOff or Stopped.

field type notes error null or Error

docs.title: Author
docs.text:
• "Provider" or "Tools" or "Core"
  • {"Frontend": string}
  • {"Extension": string}

docs.title: Body
docs.text:
• {"System": string}
  • {"User": string}
  • {"Assistant": {"finish_reason"?: string or null, "meta"?: string or null, "parts": array of Part, "stop": Stop}}
  • finish_reason: The provider's own finish string, verbatim; null when it sent none (an interrupted reply, a failed sample).
  • meta: What the response carried besides its parts (model, id, usage...), as JSON object text. Opaque to core; null when the provider sent none.
  • {"Results": array of [string, Outcome, Author]}: One (call id, outcome, by) per call, in call order. by is who produced that outcome: Tools, or the extension that answered or edited it.
  • {"Config": Config}
  • {"Custom": {"data": string, "kind": string}}

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
A config snapshot. data is opaque to core and typed by the driver.

field type notes data string

docs.title: Ending
docs.text:
How a step ended. Serde-encoded as the nodes are: it crosses the wire in a CursorView.

  • "Done" or "Aborted"
  • {"Halted": string}
  • {"Failed": string}

docs.title: Error
docs.text:
A JSON-RPC error object; data holds what a row needs to rebuild its exception (ProtocolMismatch: server; UnknownCommand: name).

field type notes code ErrorCode message string data object optional

docs.title: Form
docs.text:
What a client knows of something it fills in: a command (its name, typed as /name, its description and the schema of its arguments, with the named types' "format" and each default, and the extension that owns it) or an extension's options (the name of the extension, and a schema whose defaults are the values now; extension is null, as it is for /config). A command is called by its qualified name, extension:name, which on the wire a client writes itself from the two fields. A command that yields gives its bare name up to any other command that has it (/model stays the built-in's; the yielding one is only /skills:model). Frozen, compared by value, and not hashable: the schema is a dict.

field type notes name string description string schema object extension string or null optional yields boolean optional

docs.title: HookFailure
docs.text:
A cursor hook of extension raised, or broke its contract, at hook point ("pre_step", "post_step", ...). error is "Type: msg", the text a post_step hook sees in Ending.Failed.

field type notes extension string point string error string

docs.title: Item
docs.text: field type notes data ItemData id integer to integer

docs.title: ItemData
docs.text:
• {"Input": {"by": Author, "text": string}}
  • {"Extension": {"data": string, "name": string}}

docs.title: Node
docs.text: field type notes body Body by Author copied_from integer or null optional, The node this one repeats verbatim (a compaction or prune copy). A log written before this field existed has none. delivers array of integer derived_from integer or null optional, The node whose walk this one's content was computed from (a summary, a pruned transcript). A log written before this field existed has none. id integer parent integer or null optional time integer typed string or null optional, What a person typed, for a User node whose text a pre_input hook changed (the attachments extension inlines files). Set only when it differs from the text: the node's body is what the model sees, this is what to put back in an editor. A log written before this field existed has none.

docs.title: OpenQuestion
docs.text:
A question an extension asked and nobody has answered: id (what answer names), whom it is for (to: a client id, null for anyone), the extension that asked, what it asks, and the JSON Schema of the answer.

field type notes id integer to string or null extension string text string schema object

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
• "Interrupted"
  • {"Ok": string}
  • {"Err": string}

docs.title: Parsed
docs.text:
A command line, read: the command form, its args (decoded JSON), and the missing required parameters, in order, which a frontend asks for. For /config <extension> the command is the extension's options form, args the options to change and extension its name; with no args the line asks for the form, which a frontend shows from Client.options. save is whether --save was typed. run makes the call.

field type notes command Form args object missing array of string extension string or null optional save boolean optional

docs.title: Part
docs.text:
One piece of a reply. replay is null unless the provider kept data to send back. Logs written before replay existed load as null.

  • {"Text": Prose}
  • {"Thinking": Prose}
  • {"Call": {"args_raw": string, "id": string, "replay"?: Replay, "tool": string}}

docs.title: Prose
docs.text:
A string is plain; an object is signed. Deserialized by hand because untagged would drop the reason a bad replay was refused.

One of: string or {"replay": Replay, "text": string}

docs.title: Replay
docs.text:
Data only the provider that wrote a part can send back (a signature, a redacted block). data is the text of a JSON object with no repeated key, kept exactly as given and opaque to core beyond that; provider names who may send it back.

field type notes data string provider string

docs.title: Stop
docs.text: One of: "End" or "Tools" or "Length" or "Interrupted" or "Error"

docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
What hello answers: the protocol the server speaks, its τ version, the session id it serves, the cwd that session runs in (paths complete there), and its pid.

field type notes protocol integer version string session string cwd string pid integer

The error table (D21 section 5).

docs.title: Tau 0.16 preview API: The wire
docs.text:
Unreleased

Generated from the docstrings of Tau 0.16.0-dev (commit c439c401) by scripts/api_docs.py in the Tau repository. Not the 0.15 API.

docs.title: The wire
docs.text:
tau serve and the remote client.

Names: Json, PROTOCOL, ProtocolError, ProtocolMismatch, Server, Welcome

docs.title: Json
docs.text:
Json = dict[str, object]

A JSON object as Python holds it: what a schema or a decoded JSON object is typed as.

docs.title: PROTOCOL
docs.text:
PROTOCOL: Final = 1

The wire protocol's version. D12: a version marks a released protocol. It goes up by one at a release whose docs/protocol.schema.json differs from the last tag's, never per commit.

docs.title: ProtocolError
docs.text:
class ProtocolError(RuntimeError)

The other end broke the protocol: a message that is not JSON-RPC, a method that does not exist, a value that does not fit. Not a ConnectionError: connecting again would not help.

docs.title: ProtocolMismatch
docs.text:
class ProtocolMismatch(ProtocolError)

hello named a protocol the server does not speak. server is the one it does.

docs.title: ProtocolMismatch.init
docs.text: def __init__(self, message: str, server: int) -> None

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
class Server

A session's Driver served on a Unix socket (the module docstring). start binds path; welcome is what hello answers. wait returns when the driver has failed, or (with idle) when no client has been connected and every cursor at rest for that many seconds; close lets the connections say end (stop the driver first) and unbinds.

docs.title: Server.init
docs.text: def __init__(self, driver: Driver, path: Path, welcome: Welcome, idle: float | None = None) -> None

docs.title: Server.start
docs.text:
@classmethod
async def start(
    cls,
    driver: Driver,
    path: Path,
    *,
    session: str,
    cwd: Path,
    idle: float | None = None,
) -> 'Server'

Serve driver (running, in the loop) at path, as session session in cwd. idle seconds is how long wait lets the server rest before it returns (None: never). OSError if the socket cannot be bound.

docs.title: Server.wait
docs.text:
async def wait(self) -> Exception | None

Wait until the driver has failed (returns its failure) or stopped, or, for a server with idle, has rested that long (returns None).

docs.title: Server.close
docs.text:
async def close(self) -> None

Let the connections finish (the driver should be stopped, so each has said end; one that has not in GRACE seconds is closed), then unbind. A call a connection began and left is cancelled.

docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Welcome
    protocol: int
    version: str
    session: str
    cwd: str
    pid: int

What hello answers: the protocol the server speaks, its τ version, the session id it serves, the cwd that session runs in (paths complete there), and its pid.

docs.title: Tau — Reference
docs.text:
Cognition × Application

Four importable packages, five distributions (Python 3.12 or newer), three wire protocols, one extension API. This page is the map; each package has its own page below it.

Draft

Built for lookup, not narrative reading. Written against the running code rather than against the source repo's own design docs, several of which predate the current provider layer. Checked against v0.15.0. tau --help is the exact contract for every CLI table here; treat a disagreement as this page being stale.

docs.title: The stack
docs.text: The four packages and the one-way boundaryFour labelled boxes stacked down the left of the figure, each with a gloss to its right, and one red horizontal rule across the whole width. At the top, above the rule, sits tau underscore coding underscore agent, glossed as the tau command and the Textual TUI, and noted that c l i dot p y imports the app only inside its launch functions so that tau dash p and tau dash dash mode r p c load no interface library. The red rule below it is marked the one-way boundary, with the gloss that nothing below the line imports anything above it. Under the rule are three more boxes. tau underscore agent underscore core holds the agent loop, tools, sessions and extensions, and assumes no terminal. tau underscore jmfts, drawn in a lighter outline because it is optional, sends an arrow up into tau underscore agent underscore core. tau underscore llm sits at the bottom holding the three wire protocols and the message, tool and streaming-event types, and depends on pydantic and httpx and nothing else. A downward arrow runs from the coding agent across the red rule into the agent core, and a second downward arrow runs from the agent core past the jmfts box into tau underscore llm. Every arrow points down; none points up.interfacetau_coding_agentthe tau command, and the Textual TUIcli.py imports the app only inside its launch functions,so tau -p loads no interface librarythe one-way boundarynothing below this line imports anything above itheadlesstau_agent_corethe agent loop, tools, sessions, extensionsno textual, no stdin or stdout assumptionstau_jmftsoptional · --store jmftsan entry becomes a documenttau_llmthree wire protocols, and the message,tool and streaming-event typesdepends on pydantic and httpx, nothing elseRead the arrows as "imports". Every one points down, and the red rule is the reason the split is worth having rather than a filing convention: because nothing under it reaches up, the headless half runs with no terminal libraries installed at all — measured at 15 packages and 13 MB, against 27 and 31 MB with [tui]. The same property is what lets tau_agent_core be embedded in a host process, driven over stdio, or run under the TUI without knowing which.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
Each is installable on its own. The ffwf- prefix is not decoration: tau-ai and tau on PyPI are unrelated third-party projects (an unprefixed tau-llm does not exist there), so an install command missing the prefix fetches someone else's code or nothing.

Distribution Imports as What it is ffwf-tau — The guessable name. A meta package, no code of its own: depends on ffwf-tau-coding-agent[tui], ffwf-tau-agent-core[images] and ffwf-tau-llm[anthropic,google], all at the same version. ffwf-tau-llm tau_llm Wire protocols, message and tool types, streaming events. ffwf-tau-agent-core tau_agent_core Agent loop, tools, sessions, extensions, RPC. Headless. ffwf-tau-coding-agent tau_coding_agent The tau command and the Textual TUI. ffwf-tau-jmfts tau_jmfts JMFTS-backed session store. See Tau + JMFTS.

The meta package is the front door — the guessable name, and it pins all three layers at the same version. It installs everything that works on its own: the TUI, the Anthropic and Google SDKs, and Pillow for image reads:

pip install ffwf-tau

Installing the top of the stack directly pulls the rest:

pip install 'ffwf-tau-coding-agent[tui]'

The meta deliberately does not pull [jmfts] — that store needs a running server, so it stays an opt-in extra — nor the daemon: ffwf-tau[serve] adds tau serve and tau --connect.

Everything past the headless core is an extra, and each one reports its own absence with the install command rather than a traceback:

Extra Adds Needed for ffwf-tau-coding-agent[tui] textual, rich the interactive TUI. tau -p, tau --mode rpc and tau --mode repl run a full turn without it. ffwf-tau-coding-agent[repl] rich, prompt_toolkit tau --mode repl, the prompt-line head. Separate from [tui] because it needs no Textual. ffwf-tau-coding-agent[jmfts] ffwf-tau-jmfts --store jmfts. ffwf-tau-coding-agent[serve] (or ffwf-tau[serve]) websockets tau serve and tau --connect. ffwf-tau-agent-core[images] Pillow the read tool on an image. ffwf-tau-agent-core[codemode-monty] pydantic-monty the Monty interpreter for the experimental code-mode extension. ffwf-tau-llm[tokenizers] tokenizers exact token counting in tau_llm.tokens instead of the character-class estimate. ffwf-tau-agent-core[bus] nats-py the built-in nats_bus extension. ffwf-tau-agent-core[testing] pytest importing tau_agent_core.testing. ffwf-tau-llm[anthropic] anthropic calling Anthropic (api: "anthropic-messages"). ffwf-tau-llm[google] google-genai calling Gemini or Gemma (api: "google-generative-ai").

The two vendor SDKs import lazily, on the first request rather than at module import, so a plain install pulls neither and import tau_llm works without them.

The install puts two console scripts on PATH — tau and ffwf-tau, the same entry point behind each. Type tau; write ffwf-tau in scripts, systemd units and Dockerfiles. See the DevOps Manual for why.

docs.title: Where each subject lives
docs.text:
Page Covers tau_llm The three wire protocols, the two registries and the pool, Model, message and content types, streaming events, tool definitions, reasoning signatures. tau_agent_core The turn loop and its two event vocabularies, submit() and the one door, sessions as a tree, the SDK entry point, project context files, compaction. Extensions The ExtensionAPI surface, the hook vocabulary, discovery and collision rules, the bus capability grant. RPC The JSON-RPC verb tables, the two answers a submission gets, reading the conversation tree over the wire, and the seven verbs τ declines. tau_coding_agent The run modes, tau serve, the full CLI flag table, config.json, and what the TUI is actually made of. API Every name, its signature, its parameters — generated from the source's own docstrings rather than written here.

The five pages above are prose: they say how the pieces fit and which distinctions are easy to get backwards. API is the other kind of reference — one entry per marked object, exported from the τ repository by a script, so it says what the code says and no more.

docs.title: Three things that are easy to get backwards
docs.text:
A tool call is transformed four times on its way from HTTP bytes to a rendered widget — provider ToolCall, then a message dict block, then a backend info dict, then a widget. When tool calling misbehaves, trace the arguments value through all four hops rather than reading any one of them. tau_llm and tau_agent_core each own two of those hops.

api and provider are different questions. api is which wire protocol to speak; provider is which vendor, and therefore which base URL and which credential. Many vendors share one protocol, which is why they are two fields and two registries. See tau_llm.

Tool argument validation is hand-rolled. validate_tool_arguments checks type and required from a plain-dict schema and nothing else — no minLength, no minimum, no enum. Writing one of those into a tool schema looks enforced and is silently ignored. See tau_llm.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text:
Cognition × Application

Plain Python modules — importlib, no compile step, no manifest language. A module exposes def register(api): ... and api is an ExtensionAPI. The parameter is conventionally named api.

Lives in tau_agent_core, so extensions work headlessly, under the TUI, and over RPC without knowing which. Python 3.12 or later.

docs.title: Two vocabularies, two handler contracts
docs.text:
api.on(name, handler) subscribes to both kinds, and routes by name. The name you subscribe to therefore decides which contract you owe.

A mutating hook returns a value; a notify event does notA turn runs left to right along a horizontal spine through four stages: input, tool underscore call, tool underscore result and turn underscore end. Above the spine, under the heading mutating hooks, the return value is applied, sits a box reading handler with the arguments event and c t x, glossed that event is a plain dict. A plain arrow runs up from the tool underscore call stage into that handler, and a red arrow runs back down from the handler into the same stage, squared off in red where it leaves the handler. The red mark beside it reads the return is applied, glossed veto the call or patch its arguments. Below the spine, under the heading notify-only events, observer, cannot block, a wider box reads api dot on of all, or AgentSession dot subscribe, where the event is an AgentEvent object. Two faint arrows drop into it from the tool underscore call and tool underscore result stages, and neither returns.mutating hooks — the return value is appliedhandler(event, ctx)event is a plain dictthe return is appliedveto the call, or patch its argumentsinputtool_calltool_resultturn_endnotify-only events — observer, cannot blockapi.on("all")or AgentSession.subscribe() — event is an AgentEventOne call, api.on, two contracts. Red marks the arrow that comes back, because that is the whole distinction: a mutating hook's return value is applied to the turn, so its handler takes (event, ctx) and gets a plain dict. A notify handler takes one argument and gets an AgentEvent object, and nothing it returns is read. Subscribing to a hook with a one-argument handler raises TypeError the first time it fires — which for tool_call blocks that call and ends the turn. Kind Handler event is mutating hook, lifecycle hook handler(event, ctx) a plain dict notify-only event handler(event) an AgentEvent object

Mutating hooks — the return value is applied:

Hook What returning a value does tool_call veto the call, or patch its arguments, before execution tool_result modify content or details, or terminate, after execution before_agent_start contribute to the system prompt input transform the user prompt; {"handled": True} consumes it without a turn, {"refuse": "<reason>"} refuses the submission (submit reports accepted=False with that reason and writes nothing) turn_end return {message} for a durable append before the next request user_turn_end return {message} for a durable append session_before_switch veto a session new, fork or switch operation annotate return JSON, stored on the message entry about to be written as ext[<extension name>] and never sent to the model. At most one handler per extension entry_written observe {kind, entry_id, message, blocks} for each message entry after it is in the store (a deep copy; the return is ignored). Not dispatched when store_history is off turn_setting_changed observe {cursor_id, setting, old, new, source} when a model or thinking change is recorded (return ignored)

Lifecycle hooks — session_start, session_shutdown. Each carries a reason, for example "reload".

Notify-only events — every AgentEvent type: agent_start, agent_end, turn_start, message_start / message_update / message_end, tool_execution_start / tool_execution_update / tool_execution_end, side_completion_start / _update / _end, provider_retry, follow_ups_dropped, suspension_open / suspension_closed and lock_changed, plus the wildcard "all".

docs.title: A raising handler
docs.text: A hook whose result can change what the turn does ends the turn when its handler raises: input, before_agent_start, tool_call, tool_result, turn_end, user_turn_end, session_before_switch and annotate. The error reaches the error listeners first, and agent_end then carries end_reason: "error" naming your extension and the hook (HookHandlerError). For tool_call the failing call is answered with its block text, every other call in the batch is answered as aborted, and none runs. A raise at entry_written, turn_setting_changed, session_start or session_shutdown is reported and the turn goes on. session_before_switch has no turn: its failure means the swap does not happen and the new_session, fork or switch_session call raises. turn_end ends the turn even for a handler that only observes, so use "all" or AgentSession.subscribe() for pure observation. An unpoliced handler has no deadline.

docs.title: Handler policies
docs.text:
api.on(event, handler, policy=NAME) runs a handler under a policy that decides its deadline and what its failure becomes. gating, advisory and human are built in, and api.register_policy(name, policy) adds one (a policy is anything with async run(call, site)). A policy applies to a mutating or lifecycle hook or an ext: channel, never a notify event. Under a policy a plain def handler runs on a worker thread and the hook returns at the deadline; gating fails on timeout (which ends the turn) and advisory proceeds and sets a policy:<hook> warning. Policies are experimental below 1.0.

Handlers must not block. With no policy a handler runs inline on the event loop, so a sleep() or a slow call inside it stalls the agent. Give anything slow or remote a timeout policy.

docs.title: Two sharp edges
docs.text:
Choose the turn-boundary hook by cadence. turn_end fires once per agent-loop turn, so one user request resolved in six tool round-trips fires it six times. user_turn_end fires once per prompt(). Anything that should happen once per thing-the-user-asked-for wants the latter.

api.on("turn_end", ...) always resolves to the mutating hook, never the notify event of the same name. There is no way to observe a plain notify-grade turn_end through api.on — use "all" or AgentSession.subscribe(). context was a hook in an earlier design and is retired: calling api.on("context", ...) raises.

docs.title: The ExtensionAPI surface
docs.text:
# Events — a mutating hook or a notify event through the same call.
# Returns an unsubscribe callable.
api.on(event: str, handler: Callable, *, policy: str | None = None) -> Callable[[], None]

# Tools
api.register_tool(definition: dict | ExtensionToolDefinition) -> None
api.get_all_tools() -> list[Any]
api.set_active_tools(names: list[str]) -> None

# Commands and shortcuts
api.register_command(name: str, command: dict) -> str | None   # None, or the qualified name that holds it
api.get_command(name: str) -> dict | None
await api.run_command(name: str, args: str = "")   # wrap or defer to another command
api.unregister_command(name: str) -> None
api.register_shortcut(key: str, command: str, *, args: str = "",
                      description: str | None = None) -> None   # ctrl+e <key>

# A command that declares what it TAKES, so every head can complete and ask for it
api.register_flow(name: str, description: str, handler, *,
                  argument=None, domain=None, values=None) -> str | None

# Put a request in front of whoever is attached; optionally lock the session
api.request_user_action(sentence: str, *, lock: bool = False,
                        ask: dict | None = None,
                        release: str | None = None) -> str

# Session state
api.append_entry(custom_type: str, data: dict) -> None   # durable, not RAM-only
api.set_session_name(name: str) -> None
api.get_session_name() -> str | None

# Messaging
api.send_user_message(content: str, deliver_as: str = "followUp") -> None
api.send_message(message: dict, options: dict | None = None) -> None

# Turn origination — the one door, for extensions
await api.submit(...)
api.submit_threadsafe(...)

# Inter-extension pub/sub, on ext:<name>:<topic> channels
await api.emit(topic: str, payload: Any) -> None
await api.request(topic: str, payload: Any, *, timeout_s: float) -> list[RequestReply]
api.subscriber_count(topic: str) -> int

# Waiting for an answer (step-debugger suspensions)
await api.suspend(spec: dict) -> dict
api.can_suspend() -> bool ; api.can_suspend_here() -> bool ; api.suspend_refusal() -> str | None
api.resumed() -> dict | None

# Handler policies
api.register_policy(name: str, policy) -> None

# Warnings that persist until cleared
api.set_warning(key: str, message: str, severity: str = "warning") -> None
api.clear_warning(key: str) -> None

# Per-extension config
api.config -> dict[str, Any]

api.ui      -> ExtensionUI
api.context -> ExtensionContext

api.config is sourced from ~/.tau/config.json's extensions.<name> block, keyed by the extension's identifier (a drop-in's file stem, an installed package's module name), and overridable per run with --ext-config NAME:KEY=VALUE, where the CLI wins. The value is JSON-decoded when it parses (budget:ceiling=5.0), else it is a string. It replaces register_flag and get_flag, which were deleted rather than deprecated — they never populated a value.

A module may declare CONFIG_SCHEMA, a ui.form spec ({title, fields}) naming the keys api.config may hold. It is validated at load; an invalid one raises ExtensionCapabilityError and register never runs. The RPC verbs get_extension_config and set_extension_config read and write against it. Values set that way last for the session and are not written to config.json.

send_user_message's default is "followUp", not "steer". The other valid values are "nextTurn" and "steer".

docs.title: register_tool takes a plain dict
docs.text:
Not a ToolDefinition. tau_llm.define_tool() exists and is validated, but it builds the other tool shape: its execute takes the tool's own parameters, while an extension tool's execute is execute(tool_call_id, params, signal, on_update, ctx) and receives the bound ExtensionContext.

register_tool will not accept a ToolDefinition, and that is deliberate — the two contracts are not interchangeable. See tau_llm.

ExtensionAPI.register_tool() does default label to name, where define_tool refuses to. That is a pi-compatible contract, not an inconsistency to harmonise away.

docs.title: Discovery, authorization and collisions
docs.text:
Finding is not loading. τ discovers two kinds of source and loads one only once it is authorized:

  • drop-ins in ~/.tau/extensions/, bare *.py files or <dir>/__init__.py packages, alphabetically. The identifier is the file stem.
  • installed packages that declare an entry point in the tau.extensions group, naming a module that exposes register(api):
[project.entry-points."tau.extensions"]
planner = "tau_router.planner"

The identifier is the module name (tau_router.planner).

An unauthorized source is offered in the TUI and named on stderr by the headless modes, which never prompt. The tau ext subcommands manage this: list (every source found and whether it would load; imports nothing), authorize, revoke, disable and enable. A package's authorization record names its distribution and version, so a new version asks again. Drop-ins present at the first 0.14.0 start were authorized once, automatically. A discovered extension that fails to load gets one notice and the run goes on; tau ext disable silences it.

Every explicit -e / --extension PATH|MODULE is authorized by being named. It is repeatable, a value holding a / or ending in .py is a path and anything else an installed module, and it loads even under --no-extensions, which disables discovery only. An explicitly named extension that fails to load stops startup in -p and --mode rpc.

There is no project-local <cwd>/.tau/extensions/ discovery, and no dependency-manifest convention inside an extension directory. The first is deferred pending a trust gate rather than overlooked: a repository you cloned should not be able to run code by being opened.

Collision handling differs by kind, on purpose:

Kind On a duplicate tool raises ValueError at load time command first-wins on the typed name. The loser keeps its qualified name ext:<extension>:<command>, and register_command returns it shortcut last-write-wins, with a logged warning tool_call hook chain the first block: True wins before_agent_start system prompt last contribution wins

docs.title: Asking the user, and locking the session
docs.text:
api.request_user_action appends one reserved extension_request entry to the session. That is what makes it different from a modal: it is on the record, it survives a restart, and every head renders it — the TUI, the REPL, and an RPC host through get_pending_request / answer_request.

Two keys give four states. lock=True refuses further submissions until the request is answered; ask is a form spec ({title, fields, actions}) that draws a control rather than a sentence. A request with neither is a notice; one with both is a locked question. release names a command that clears the lock — a command is exempt from a lock by placement in the pipeline, not by name.

Raise a request where nothing appends after it — user_turn_end, session_start, or a command handler. A tool_call hook is mid-turn, so its request ends up several entries behind the leaf and the cursor never reaches it. api.suspend is the in-process cousin: it pauses the turn and waits for a responder (a head, or an RPC host that has sent declare_capabilities), from tool_call, entry_written, turn_end or user_turn_end. See RPC. examples/44_release_gate.py is the worked demo, and examples/30_permission_gate.py is the human-in-the-loop bash gate.

docs.title: Headless dialogs raise
docs.text:
ctx.ui.form raises HeadlessDialogError in headless mode unless a policy is configured — --ui-defaults form=defaults or config.json's ui_defaults. A dialog that quietly picked a default would make an unattended run's result depend on a question nobody saw.

confirm, select and input no longer exist. Each is replaced by a field on an ask — a confirm field, a select field, a text field. They are named rather than silently dropped: --ui-defaults confirm=yes in an old script is refused with the replacement named, instead of parsing into a policy that governs nothing.

docs.title: The bus capability grant
docs.text:
An extension that touches a message bus declares TOUCHES_BUS = True and is refused at load time unless the run opts in with --bus (CLI) or bus_available=True (SDK). It is a capability grant, not a default.

The declaration has a second half: such an extension must also declare a non-empty SUBJECTS, naming what it touches. Leaving it unset is refused even with --bus given, because the grant is per-subject rather than blanket.

The shipped example is nats_bus.py, which needs pip install 'ffwf-tau-agent-core[bus]' for its NATS client.

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
Cognition × Application

tau --mode rpc speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, newline-delimited. τ as a process a host drives, rather than a library it imports.

Forty-five verbs are implemented. Seven more are formally declined, each with a stated reason, rather than silently absent. (The count is printed in the generated reference, docs/RPC-PROTOCOL.md, which is the place to cite it from.) Eighteen event types are pushed.

Protocol version 3.1. protocol_version is MAJOR.MINOR: MAJOR bumps when something already on the wire breaks, MINOR when the change is purely additive. A client must ignore any field, and any event type, it does not recognise.

tau --mode rpc is one of two out-of-process doors. tau serve is a daemon that speaks a different protocol, with its own version, over WebSocket (JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per frame) and a hello handshake; 39 of its requests are these same RPC verbs. Its error codes share one table with RPC, so -32005, -32006 and -32007 appear below but are never sent over stdio. This page covers the stdio protocol only.

docs.title: A submission answers twice
docs.text: Two answers on acceptance, one on rejectionTwo panels divided by a vertical rule. The left panel is headed accepted. A host lifeline and a tau lifeline run down it. The host sends submit across to tau; tau answers back with accepted. A thicker segment of the tau lifeline below that is glossed the turn runs. Then a red arrow crosses back from tau to the host, squared off in red where it leaves the lifeline, and is marked the second answer, glossed agent underscore end, when the turn ends. The right panel is headed rejected. The host again sends submit, and tau answers once with error minus 32000, SUBMISSION underscore REJECTED. Beneath it the panel notes there is no later event, and that the error is the answer.acceptedhosttausubmitacceptedthe turn runsthe second answeragent_end, when the turn endsrejectedhosttausubmit-32000 SUBMISSION_REJECTEDno later event followsthe error is the whole answerThe shape a host has to code for. submit and prompt return immediately with an acceptance, and the result of the turn arrives later as a notification — red, because a host that treats the first response as the answer will sit waiting for a turn that already finished. A rejected submission inverts it: the error arrives on the response and nothing follows, so a host waiting for agent_end after a rejection waits forever.

docs.title: Verbs
docs.text:
Tier Verbs A — turn and state (10) prompt · abort · get_state · get_messages · get_commands · get_tools · get_capabilities · new_session · fork · switch_session B — session management (10) compact · set_model · get_models · set_session_name · get_session_name · get_session_stats · list_sessions · set_auto_compaction · get_last_assistant_text · complete_path C — the tree, the extensions, and provenance (25) submit · set_reasoning · navigate · get_tree · get_entry · elide_span · commit_branch · paste_subtree · summarize_and_navigate · complete_message_id · next_step · enumerate_domain · get_pending_request · answer_request · get_pending_suspensions · answer_suspension · declare_capabilities · enable_extension · disable_extension · reload_extension · list_managed_extensions · list_extensions · get_extension_state · get_extension_config · set_extension_config

submit is Tier C rather than Tier A because it is τ's own verb rather than one any harness has: it stamps submission_id · source · submitter · correlation on every event the turn produces, so a host multiplexing agents can say which subject a prompt came from and get it back on each event.

Verbs new since 0.10: set_reasoning names a thinking level (0.13.0, the one path the TUI's /thinking and an extension's ctx.set_reasoning also use); list_extensions lists what tau ext list lists, including extensions found but not loaded (unauthorized, unusable, colliding), and authorizing one is deliberately not a wire verb; get_pending_suspensions, answer_suspension and declare_capabilities are the step-debugger verbs (0.15.0, see below).

Call get_capabilities first on a new connection, and check protocol_version before sending anything mutating. It publishes the verb list, the event schema, declined[], and limits.max_request_line_bytes.

Give your own subprocess reader an 8 MiB line limit before that call — get_capabilities's own response is tens of kilobytes, well over the stdlib StreamReader default of 64 KiB.

docs.title: The seven declined verbs
docs.text:
Each is reachable through get_capabilities().declined[]. Calling one returns -32601 METHOD_NOT_FOUND; the published reason, not the bare error, is how a host learns why.

Verb Why declined send_tool_result τ's loop executes tool calls itself. Accepting a result over RPC opens a second, unauthenticated path into the same executor that a host never drove the call for. bash The same reasoning. τ's bash is a tool the loop runs under a submission's provenance and admission rules; an out-of-band shell verb bypasses both. cycle_model A keybinding affordance, not a protocol verb. A host names a model with set_model rather than stepping through a list it cannot see. cycle_thinking_level The same judgment: a keybinding-shaped "next level". A host names the level with set_reasoning. set_steering_mode multitask_strategy is already a per-submission parameter on submit and prompt, not a session-wide mode to toggle. set_follow_up_mode The same — multitask_strategy="enqueue" covers it per call. export_html Rendering is the host's job. τ hands back get_messages and events. (The TUI and CLI do export HTML; this wire does not.)

Two of these share one principle worth stating plainly: a second privileged path into the same executor is a second thing to secure.

docs.title: Reading the tree
docs.text:
get_tree returns every entry in the log in the order a browser draws them — preorder over the parent/child tree, roots in load order, children oldest first.

It is flat, with parent_id carrying the shape. A nested projection of a five-hundred-message linear conversation is five hundred levels of nesting, which is a serializer's recursion limit rather than a tree anyone wanted. It is also unbounded: the shape is the answer, and a bounded shape is a different tree. count is there so a host can say it read a whole one.

Each row is wider than the tree node it comes from, because drawing a tree and colouring one need different facts:

Field What reads it entry_id every message_id argument — navigate, elide_span, commit_branch, paste_subtree, summarize_and_navigate parent_id the shape; null for a root role, preview, is_leaf, timestamp what a row is drawn from: the message role (null on bookkeeping kinds), the first line uncut, whether it is the head cursor's leaf, and the key children are sorted by kind message, customMessage, compaction, elide, branch_summary, navigate, customEntry, model_change. Not a closed enum — a kind added later arrives as a row a host can draw and does not recognise, rather than as a gap first_kept_id a fold's boundary: which entries it covers tool_call_ids / tool_call_id the call/result pairing a selection expands over copyable whether paste_subtree takes this row as a source from_id a branch summary and the line it is about is_system the prompt a fold carries across rather than dropping estimated_tokens a selection readout — an estimate, and says so

The result also carries leaf, count, and side: session-level side entries (a suspension opened before the first entry), which never appear as root rows.

Nothing is filtered out. Which rows a browser declines to draw — a navigate with one child, say — is the reader's rule, not the log's.

get_entry returns one entry's full body by id, raw, in its stored camelCase shape (parentId, firstKeptId, fromId). get_messages does not serve this: it answers for the active path, and the node a browser's cursor sits on is very often not on it. The pair is what a detail pane needs — a one-line preview per row from get_tree, and the body of the one node being shown.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Every event is a type: "event" notification with a fixed record shape: unpopulated fields are null or false, never omitted. No unbounded field is pushed. message_update carries a bounded delta (with block_type and a replace flag that means "reset your accumulator"), never the cumulative message, and agent_end carries message_count and the resulting leaf; pull the messages with get_messages. The types are the twelve loop events, the side_completion_* triple, provider_retry, follow_ups_dropped, suspension_open, suspension_closed and lock_changed; see tau_agent_core.

What a host should read off them:

  • agent_end.end_reason says how a turn stopped (done, terminate, aborted, max_turns, repeat_tool_calls, error, suspended), and error_detail gives type, status, retry_after, headers and retryable for a provider failure. A stop_reason of length on message_end means the output cap cut the content off.
  • compact answers twice, like submit: an immediate {accepted, compaction_id}, then a compaction_end notification. That notification is its own method, not an event; a host that treats every other notification as a violation will see compact never finish.
  • message_end carries reasoning_level (the level actually sent, after the provider clamped it), response_headers, and dropped_tool_calls.

docs.title: Suspensions
docs.text: An extension can pause a turn with api.suspend and wait for a responder. On RPC the host is that responder only if it says so: declare_capabilities with suspensions: true. A host that never declares gets NoResponderError from every api.suspend, because a wait on a channel nobody sits on would hang the turn. suspension_open and suspension_closed events carry the suspension and its resolution; get_pending_suspensions is the snapshot to read after starting; answer_suspension takes the first valid answer, and a later one gets accepted: false rather than an error. These verbs, with abort and get_state, run in a control lane that is served while a request is waiting on a suspension.

docs.title: The lock a host can release
docs.text:
An extension can put a request in front of whoever is attached, and can lock the session until it is answered. get_pending_request is the read a host makes at every cursor move; null is the ordinary answer and is not a failure.

A request carries {entry_id, extension, extension_name, sentence, label, lock, ask, release}. sentence is the extension's own line; label is τ's framing of the four states over lock and ask, shipped rather than derived so a host does not hold a second copy of that table; ask is a validated form spec ({title, fields, actions}) or null; release names a command that clears the lock.

answer_request appends the response and then dispatches the pressed action, in that order, so the handler runs on a session that is already unlocked. The append is what releases the lock — a lock is read at the cursor, and appending moves the cursor — which is why the result carries cursor as the evidence the session is answerable again.

handled: false is a warning, not a failure: the extension that raised the request is not loaded, nothing ran, and the lock is gone anyway. A lock whose owner cannot answer must not become a session nobody can continue.

docs.title: Where an RPC session lives
docs.text:
--mode rpc defaults its session base to a private <tmp>/.tau-<uid>/sessions rather than ~/.tau/sessions. A subprocess a host spawns and tears down should not litter the shared directory.

The consequence is that a host and the human at the terminal are normally looking at different session lists. --session-dir DIR is how a host joins the user's. list_sessions returns scope: {store, cwd} precisely so a host can tell which universe it is in, and its listing and switch_session's resolution are the same set by construction — an id this verb returns is an id that verb accepts.

docs.title: Why a host might prefer RPC to embedding
docs.text:
A subprocess gives a host one property an in-process import cannot: a real hard kill. terminate() and kill() against a τ child work the way they work against any subprocess, so a runaway tool-call loop is stoppable from outside rather than only cooperatively.

The reader loop is serial apart from a small control lane (abort, get_state, answer_suspension, get_pending_suspensions), so abort stays answerable while a turn is in flight — measured at get_state answering in 0.44s and abort in 0.46s against a 20-second provider call.

Embedding trades that away. abort becomes cooperative only, and a wedged tool or a CPU-bound stretch shares the host's event loop.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Beyond JSON-RPC's own -32700 to -32603, τ defines -32000 SUBMISSION_REJECTED, -32001 COMMAND_NOT_SUPPORTED, -32002 TURN_STILL_RUNNING (a new_session, fork or switch_session could not stop the in-flight turn in time; nothing was touched), -32003 REQUEST_TOO_LARGE (a request line over limits.max_request_line_bytes, 8 MiB; the connection stays usable), and -32004 SESSION_NOT_PERSISTED (a verb that appends was called on a session with no durable location, as under --no-session). get_state reports addressable so a host can know before it trips this.

docs.title: The generated reference
docs.text:
docs/RPC-PROTOCOL.md in the source repo is the exact wire reference. It is generated from the real command table and event schema, and a drift test asserts the checked-in file equals its own render() output — so it cannot disagree with the code that serves it.

Treat the tables above as an index into that file, not a replacement for it.

docs.title: tau_agent_core — the runtime
docs.text:
Cognition × Application

The loop that drives a conversation, the door every input arrives through, and the tree a session actually is. Headless: no Textual, no assumptions about stdin or stdout. It runs under the TUI, in a host process, or as an RPC subprocess, and cannot tell which.

Distribution ffwf-tau-agent-core, Python 3.12 or later. It depends on tau_llm; tau_agent_core never imports tau_coding_agent.

docs.title: The agent loop
docs.text:
AgentLoop(
    config: AgentLoopConfig, emit=None, tools=None, model=None,
    abort_signal=None, hook_dispatcher=None, steer_queue=None,
    mid_turn_compactor=None, writer=None, call_gate=None,
    turn_settings=None, input_failure=None, position=None,
)

AgentLoop lives in tau_agent_core.agent_loop and is not re-exported from the package root. config, tools, model and abort_signal are constructor arguments, not fields on one shared object. AgentLoopConfig is deliberately small: model, system_prompt, system_prompt_override, tool_execution_mode, max_retries, max_turns, repeat_tool_call_limit, temperature, api_key, reasoning.

Everything an earlier design put on the config as callbacks — before_tool_call, get_steering_messages, transform_context — is injected instead. Extension hooks go through hook_dispatcher; mid-turn steering goes through a shared steer_queue; mid_turn_compactor is offered the context at each turn boundary; writer receives each message as it exists, so the loop need not hold a turn's output in memory to persist it; call_gate refuses a model-issued call by name while the tool stays declared (so the tool block and the prompt cache hold); and turn_settings is awaited before every request for its model, key, reasoning level and temperature, so a switch made between two requests reaches the second. With a turn_settings source the config's own temperature, api_key and reasoning are ignored.

max_turns defaults to None: no ceiling. pi has none either, and τ's former hardcoded 50 is gone. Set it through create_agent_session(max_turns=...) or the config. What bounds a runaway loop without one is the abort signal and repeat_tool_call_limit, which stops the loop when that many turns in a row repeat the same wholly-failing batch of tool calls (default 3; None disables it). agent_end carries end_reason: done, terminate, aborted, max_turns, repeat_tool_calls, error or suspended, so a caller can tell a truncated answer from a complete one.

docs.title: Two event vocabularies
docs.text:
This is the thing most worth understanding, because it spans four files and two sets of names that describe the same turn.

Where the provider's events become the loop's eventsThree columns. On the left, under the heading tau underscore l l m streaming events, four boxes: TextDeltaEvent, ThinkingDeltaEvent and ToolCallDeltaEvent drawn in a light outline, and DoneEvent dot final drawn in a heavier one. Each of the three light boxes sends a thin arrow right into a tall box in the middle named AgentLoop dot run. DoneEvent dot final instead sends a red connector, squared off in red where it leaves the box, which runs right then up and enters an inner box named get underscore tool underscore calls, glossed as reading off the final message. Below that inner box sits a second one named underscore execute underscore tool underscore calls, glossed sequential or parallel. On the right, under the heading tau underscore agent underscore core AgentEvents, four more boxes receive arrows from the loop: message start with update and end, tool execution start with update and end, turn start and turn end, and agent start and agent end. Beneath the left column the red mark reads what actually runs, glossed that get underscore tool underscore calls reads DoneEvent dot final and never the accumulated deltas.tau_llm streaming eventstau_agent_core AgentEventsTextDeltaEventThinkingDeltaEventToolCallDeltaEventDoneEvent.finalAgentLoop.runone turn, then loopget_tool_calls()off the final message_execute_tool_callssequential or parallelmessage_startupdate, endtool_execution_startupdate, endturn_start / turn_endagent_start / agent_endwhat actually runsget_tool_calls() reads DoneEvent.final,never the accumulated deltasThe loop consumes one vocabulary and emits another, which is why a single turn has two sets of names for the same moment. Red marks the crossing that carries execution rather than display: the three delta events exist so a reader can watch a turn happen, but the tool calls that actually run are pulled off DoneEvent.final, whose arguments the provider has already assembled and parsed. Reconstructing a call from the deltas would work until the day a server fragments differently.

A tool call is transformed four times between HTTP bytes and a rendered widget:

  1. the provider's ToolCall block, off DoneEvent.final;
  2. a message dict block {"type": "toolCall", ...} — model_dump() at the loop boundary;
  3. a backend tool_calls_info dict;
  4. a TUI widget.

When tool calling misbehaves, trace the arguments value through all four hops rather than reading any one of them.

AgentEvent.type is one of eighteen values: the twelve above (agent_*, turn_*, message_*, tool_execution_*) and six τ additions — side_completion_start/_update/_end (a compaction or branch summary, which belongs to no turn; purpose and reason say which and why), provider_retry (a request is being re-sent; attempt, max_retries, delay_seconds), follow_ups_dropped (a user abort discarded queued follow-ups and waiting enqueue submissions; dropped lists their texts), suspension_open/suspension_closed (a turn is waiting on a responder, see below), and lock_changed (this process gained or lost write access to the tree).

τ stamps provenance on turn events — submission_id, source, submitter, correlation — and cursor_id, the cursor whose turn emitted the event, because several cursors can run turns on one session at once. It adds blocked and blocked_by on tool_execution_end for extension vetoes, details there for a tool's structured facts about its own execution, error/error_detail on agent_end when the loop raised, and response_headers on the usage-bearing message_end.

docs.title: The one door
docs.text:
AgentSession.submit() is the real entry point every input source funnels through: TUI keystrokes, tau -p, the SDK, an extension, an RPC client. prompt() builds a Submission and calls submit() — it is a wrapper, not a second door.

multitask_strategy decides what happens when a submission arrives while a turn is already running. It is a policy rather than an answer improvised per caller:

Strategy Effect reject Refuse the new submission outright; rejection_reason explains why. enqueue Queue it; it runs after the current turn ends. steer Inject it into the running turn without waiting. rollback Navigate back to the pre-turn leaf and run as if from there. The running turn's output becomes an abandoned sibling branch, not a deletion. fork Branch the conversation instead of extending the active leaf.

docs.title: Sessions are a tree
docs.text:
Append-only entries, walked by parent_id. Model input for a turn is an ephemeral frame — system prompt, tool schemas — plus the exact linear path from the root to the active leaf. There is no hidden channel on either side of that.

That is what makes fork, branch and rollback ordinary operations rather than special cases, and it is why a rollback leaves the abandoned branch on disk instead of deleting it.

A store keeps entries and nothing else. The position a new entry is parented at belongs to a Cursor, and every writer holds one: a head, tau -p, an RPC client and a sub-agent are all cursors on the same tree, none privileged. Moving a cursor writes nothing, and a cursor is not durable.

Piece Role SessionLog (Protocol) The storage contract, four members: id, entries(), async append_at(parent_id, entry_type, payload) and async finalize(entry_id, payload). Cursor A position in one tree and the only thing that appends at it. It holds the typed appenders (append_message, append_custom_message, append_custom_entry, append_config, append_compaction, append_elide, append_branch_summary), move(), and the turn state: abort signal, steer, follow-up and enqueue queues. One turn runs at a time on a cursor, any number across cursors. ConversationTree Walks parent_id chains to build model input. SessionCatalog Lists and resolves sessions. File-backed or JMFTS-backed, chosen by --store file\|jmfts or the config's session_store.backend.

BranchView, open_branch() and append_navigate are gone. A sub-agent is a cursor opened with a TurnFrame (the tool subset, model, reasoning level, prompt and max_turns it runs under) rather than a second session. Config (model, reasoning, tools) is recorded in the tree as config entries, so a reopened session continues as it was.

Where a reopened tree continues is default_leaf: the newest finished entry a person's turn wrote. Entries a sub-agent wrote (source: "agent"), incomplete entries and side entries are passed over, so a session a child wrote last reopens in the main conversation.

Two entry mechanisms are new in 0.15:

  • Incomplete entries. An entry is opened with status: "incomplete" and later finalized, keeping its id and position. A session interrupted mid-message reopens at the entry before it, and the interrupted branch stays beside the retry.
  • Side entries. An entry of a kind in SIDE_KINDS (today only suspension) hangs beside its parent. It is never an ancestor of a later entry, so it is no branch, tip or leaf; is_side_entry is how a walker asks.

An annotate extension hook returns JSON for each message entry the loop writes, and τ stores it at ext[<extension name>] on that entry, in the same write. A failing annotate handler does not lose the entry: the entry is written with the failure recorded in place of the annotation, and the turn is aborted.

tau_agent_core.testing ships contract suites for both SessionCatalog and SessionLog (SessionCatalogContractTests, SessionLogContractTests). A new store costs about twenty lines of knobs to run them. SessionLog contract: several cursors may append concurrently within one process, and the store keeps each write whole with a distinct id.

One writer per stored session. A process that hosts a session for writing holds an exclusive flock on a .lock sidecar file beside it. Another process opening the same session gets a read-only replica whose writes raise SessionReadOnlyError, naming the holder; lock_changed reports the change. On a filesystem where flock excludes nothing, the session opens for writing with a warning, which sessions.allow_unlocked_fs silences.

Release note for SessionLog implementors

The branchOf lane tag is gone. It recorded who wrote an entry, while three of its four consumers wanted does this entry belong to the conversation being looked at — which is ancestry from the cursor. The two agree for a sub-agent and disagree for a fork, so a three-way fork returned three mutually exclusive alternatives as one conversation, and a two-message session counted four messages.

Session.messages and session listing walk the cursor's ancestry. subtree_text is bounded by descendants of the node the caller named rather than by write provenance. In the contract suite, one test is inverted rather than deleted: a store must not reintroduce a cursor filter.

docs.title: SDK entry point
docs.text:
def create_agent_session(
    model: str | Model | None = None, provider: str | None = None,
    base_url: str | None = None, api_key: str | None = None,
    tools: list[str] | None = None, session_log: SessionLog | None = None,
    extensions: list[Callable] | None = None, system_prompt: str | None = None,
    no_context_files: bool = False,
    thinking_level: str | None = None, cwd: str | None = None,
    tool_execution_mode: Literal["sequential", "parallel"] = "parallel",
    compaction_policy: CompactionPolicy | None = None,
    compaction_settings: CompactionSettings | None = None,
    model_resolver: Callable[[str], Model] | None = None,
    bus_available: bool = False,
    no_tools: Literal["all", "builtin"] | None = None,
    max_turns: int | None = None,
    tool_options: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    prompt_template_paths=(), no_prompt_templates: bool = False,
    skill_paths=(), no_skills: bool = False,
) -> AgentSession

model=None is the built-in default, gpt-4o. A model id that is not built in needs provider. thinking_level=None sends no reasoning control, "off" sends the provider's off form, and any other level marks the model reasoning-capable. compaction_settings and compaction_policy are mutually exclusive. The template and skill parameters are described under prompt templates and skills.

tools takes built-in name strings only — read, write, edit, bash, grep, find, ls. A custom AgentTool instance needs the AgentSession constructor directly.

There is deliberately no settings= parameter. An earlier version had one that was silently ignored, so it was removed rather than kept as a no-op; passing it raises TypeError.

no_tools is the SDK half of the CLI's two flags. "all" offers the model nothing at all; "builtin" drops the built-in set and keeps whatever extensions registered. Passing a non-empty tools= together with no_tools= raises ValueError — they ask for opposite things, and neither outranks the other at a call site. tools=None and tools=[] stay legal alongside "all", which also withholds extension-registered tools. An unknown tool name raises ValueError too.

This factory is not on the live TUI or headless path: tau_coding_agent's backend constructs AgentSession directly. What used to follow from that no longer does — the backend now calls the same prompt builder, so τ's base prompt and its context files reach the model on every path.

docs.title: Project context files
docs.text:
The system prompt is τ's base prompt, then any discovered context files, then the tool list. system_prompt replaces the base text and nothing else; setting it does not switch context files off.

Discovery takes the agent directory's file first (τ home by default), then walks every ancestor of the working directory, root-most first so the nearest file is read last. At most one file per directory, deduplicated by resolved path, first match winning among:

AGENTS.override.md   AGENTS.md   AGENTS.MD   CLAUDE.md   CLAUDE.MD

τ's own .tau/SYSTEM.md is read from the working directory only and appended last. It is deliberately not in that tuple: inside it, it would compete with a sibling AGENTS.md under the one-file-per-directory rule, so a project carrying both — which τ has always read both of — would silently lose one.

A worktree nested inside its own main repository suppresses the main repository's same-named file, so the walk does not load both.

Three departures from pi, each because Fail Early asks for it:

  • A file that is found and cannot be read raises, naming the path and the escape hatch. pi warns to stderr and continues. A prompt silently missing its project instructions looks exactly like a model ignoring them.
  • Decoding is strict. Replacing undecodable bytes turns a mis-encoded instruction file into replacement characters the model still reads as instructions.
  • Every block is wrapped in <project_instructions path="…">, so a prompt cannot carry instructions whose origin it does not state.

The walk reaches /, so a CLAUDE.md in $HOME is read on every run. --no-context-files / -nc turns discovery off, and it is run-level: a mid-session /model switch cannot hand the files back.

docs.title: Compaction
docs.text:
LLM-backed, with no fabricated-summary fallback. A compaction error raises (CompactionError) rather than silently truncating the conversation.

should_compact(context_tokens, context_window, settings) -> bool
prepare_compaction(path_entries, settings) -> CompactionPreparation | None
async def compact(preparation, model, api_key, *, custom_instructions=None,
                  thinking_level=None, on_text_delta=None) -> CompactionResult

CompactionSettings defaults: auto=True, reserve_tokens=16384, keep_recent_tokens=20000, soft_limit_ratio=0.8, and hard_limit_tokens / soft_limit_tokens unset (derived). Auto-compaction is on by default; auto was formerly called enabled. The hard limit is context_window - reserve_tokens, and the soft limit sits at soft_limit_ratio of that. Crossing the soft limit compacts at the end of a turn. Crossing the hard limit compacts inside the loop at a turn boundary, after the turn so far has been written to the tree, so a long tool-calling turn is not lost to a refused request. A manual /compact or AgentSession.compact() ignores auto.

A compaction runs outside any turn, so it is reported as side_completion_* events with reason manual or threshold, and the tokens it spent appear on side_completion_end.usage. A declared CompactionPolicy (disabled, local_summarizer or turn_cap) is for measured runs: it makes an undeclared compaction impossible rather than changing how τ compacts.

Applying one is tree surgery rather than truncation: the first kept entry is re-parented onto the compaction entry, so the summary is on the path and the compacted span is still in the tree.

docs.title: Prompt templates and skills
docs.text: create_agent_session and the CLI load prompt templates and skills from discovered locations plus explicit paths (prompt_template_paths, skill_paths); no_prompt_templates and no_skills skip discovery while explicit paths still load. See docs/PROMPT-TEMPLATES-AND-SKILLS.md in the τ source for the file formats.

docs.title: Waiting for an answer
docs.text: An extension can pause a turn with api.suspend and wait in-process for a responder's answer (a step debugger, an approval form). The session writes a suspension side entry, queues per cursor, emits suspension_open, and resolves on the first valid answer or on abort, emitting suspension_closed with a close_reason of answered, aborted, cursor_closed or abandoned. It may be called from the tool_call, entry_written, turn_end and user_turn_end hooks. A turn that unwinds at a suspension ends with end_reason suspended. Nothing resumes across a process boundary yet.

docs.title: Built-in tools
docs.text:
read, write, edit, bash, grep, find, ls. Two things ride on top as extensions rather than core tools: background, which gives any named tool a model-chosen background option plus a bg tool to check, wait on or cancel jobs, and codemode, a sandboxed scripting tool (providers cpython, monty, typescript, which per its source is prompt-only) that runs scripts which call other tools. --tools allowlists, --exclude-tools denylists, --no-builtin-tools drops the set while keeping extension-registered ones, and --no-tools offers the model nothing at all.

Extensions still load under --no-tools: hooks, commands, injections and subscriptions are untouched, and only callable tools are withheld.

See Extensions for the registration surface and RPC for driving all of this from another process.

docs.title: tau_coding_agent — the command and the TUI
docs.text:
Cognition × Application

The tau command, and the Textual interface it can launch. This is the only package that knows what a terminal is.

Distribution ffwf-tau-coding-agent, which needs Python 3.12 or newer. Its one hard dependency is ffwf-tau-agent-core. textual and rich are the [tui] extra; rich and prompt_toolkit are the separate [repl] extra, separate because needing no Textual is the whole point of that head.
